Subject:- Collection of member data for actuarial valuation.

Dear,

The valuation of the Employees’ Pension Fund is to be done annually in accordance
to the Para 32 of the Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995. The Actuary appointed for the
purpose has pointed out the deficiencies in the data made available for the actuarial
valuation. Thus, in the absence of quality and sufficient member data may result in an
incomplete and inaccurate valuation of the Employees’ Pension Fund and therefore the
collection of Member data in respect of all the existing members in a time-bound manner
and in any case latest by 30.04.2013 has become a non-negotiable Organisational

requirement.

To carry out the process of collection of members’ data, the following action plan has
been devised:-

(a) A facility will be provided to the Employers in the Employer Portal of the EPF Website
where the employer would be able to download the data in excel format populated with
the Member Id, Member Name and other data received by EPFO through ECR. The
blank data fields are required to be filled up by the employer. There will be an upload

facility provided to employer to upload the filled up data back to EPFO through the
employer Portal.

(b) The data submitted by the employer will be made available at the RO/SRO Admin Portal
wherefrom each EPFO office will download the file pertaining to their field office and
upload the same in Application Software.

(c) The data in excel format as detailed at (a) above would be provided to the employer in
the Employer Portal by 05.04.2013. The data format for filling up the blank data field is
available as annexure-II in the ECR portal.

(d) The functionality for uploading the data on employer portal is under development and
would be provided shortly. In the meantime, the employer is being requested to keep

the data ready in consonance with the annexure-II provided in the employer portal.

In order to achieve the target of collection of data by 30.04.2013, the field offices
should not only publicise the above activity among the employers through different touch
points but also use their good offices to get in direct touch with them with a view to
sensitise them to the urgency in the matter. Further, the field offices are required to monitor
the collection of the data on a daily basis using the dashboard being made available through
RO/SRO admin portal. It is, therefore, requested to take necessary action as above to

ensure the collection of data in respect of all the existing members latest by 30.04.2013.

Please acknowledge the receipt of the letter at epfo.project@epfindia.gov.in

Yours faithfully,

ANNEXURES

Handling of Transfer Claims through a revised process

Introduction:

EPFO has been receiving a lot of grievances from its members on the service
delivery aspect and it has been observed that most of the grievances have its
genesis in the transfer of accounts on change of job by the members. Although
EPFO is planning to introduce a Permanent P.F. Account Number for its members
which would provide portability of accounts, there is an emergent need to
streamline the processing of transfer claims as the introduction of a portable
number would mainly benefit the existing members on change of job. In the
absence of any available KYC documents, the old accounts of the existing
members have to be merged with the present number or Permanent Account
Number through the processing of transfer claims thus, necessitating the
smoothening of the process of transfer of accounts. This document attempts to
introduce a revised process through which a number of bottlenecks in the
processing of transfer claims can be removed and time required for the transfer
claims can be reduced.

Present process and the problem areas:

Step 1: The member submits claim through present employer to the Transferee
office. This is done to ensure the correctness of the new P.F. account number to
which the P.F. accumulations and Service details are to be transferred.

Step 2: Transferee office verifies the signatures of the present employer and
sends the physical claim to EPF office maintaining previous employers’ records
with a forwarding letter. (Problem area: Delay due to movement of
Physical claim from Transferee office to Transferor Office)

Step 3: The transfer claim is settled in the transferor office. (Problem area:
Delay on account of obtaining the Form-5 and Form -10 from the
previous employer in case the details are not available in the transferor
office)

Step 4: After settlement at the transferor office, the Annexure-K (text file and
hard copy) is generated and sent to the transferee office along with e-payment.
(Problem area: Delay in transfer of Annexure- K (text file and hard
copy) to the transferee office)

Step 5: The text file is uploaded in the transferee office, which can only be
approved after cash reconciliation. (Problem area: Delay in upload of
Annexure- K (text file) in the transferee office)

Step 6: The Annexure-K is reconciled with bank statement in the Cash section in
transferee office in each case. (Problem area: Delay in cash reconciliation
of money transfer with Bank Statement in each individual case by the
cash branch at the transferee office)

Step 7: The Accounts section approves transfer and P.F. accumulations and
service details are added to the new P.F. account of the member.

Sub: Departmental Promotion Committees (DPCs) — following Model Calendar
- Reg.

Sir,

It has come to notice of the Head Office that in many of the field offices
DPCs are not convened in accordance with the prescribed model calendar for
conduct of DPCs. The matter has been viewed seriously by the Central P.F.
Commissioner.

In this regard, reference is invited to the DoP&T’s OM dated 08.09.1998
and 11.03.2011 (copies enclosed) containing instructions which provide that
the DPCs should be convened at regular intervals to draw panels which could
be utilized for making promotions against the vacancies occurring during the
course of a year, This enjoins upon the concerned authorities to initiates action
to fill up the existing as well as anticipated vacancies well in advance of the
expiry of the previous panel by collecting relevant documents like seniority list,
ACRs etc. for placing before the DPC.

It is pertinent to mention here that delays in promotions results in
considerable frustration among the officials, thereby adversely affecting their
morale and overall productivity. As a remedial measure, the DoP&T has
prescribed a time schedule for convening DPCs with the objective of ensuring
that the prepared panel is utilized as and when the vacancies arises during the
course of a vacancy year,

Non-adherence to the time frame of DPCs is a matter of serious concern
on which the Central P.F. Commissioner has expressed his displeasure. He has
directed that the Regional Commissioner In-charge of the Region should
ensure strict adherence to the model calendar for the DPCs as prescribed by
the DoP&T vide OM dated 08.09.1998 (copy enclosed).

Yqurs faithfully,

Sub: Training Programme on Establishment & Administration - Nomination(s) - reg.

Sir,

As per Training Calendar of NATRSS for the financial year 2013-2014. The National Academy
for Training and Research in Social Security (NATRSS) is conducting a three-days Training
Programme on “Establishment & Administration” scheduled to be held from 29th April to 01st
May 2013 (3 days) in its premises at -

30-31 Institutional Area, D-Block, Janak Puri, New Delhi-110058.
The course will broadly cover the following topics:

° State and explain the provisions regarding recruitment , appointment, promotion,
seniority, pay fixation and reservation policy and its implementation

Explain the do’s and don’ts of Conduct Rules.

Explain the procedure for initiating Major Penalty and Minor Penalty.

Explain provisions governing deputation/foreign services.

Explain provisions of Rajbhasha

Explain purchase/procurement provisions.

You are requested to nominate One APFC/RPFC-II from your region. While nominating,

preference may please be given to officers who have not undergone any training programme.
It may also be ensured that no officer who is retiring in this financial year may be nominated.

The name of the nominated officer may please be communicated latest by 12 April 2013.

The accommodation in the hostel will be available from one day before the commencement of
the programme till one day after the completion of the training programme. Any extension beyond
this will require specific approval of Director, NATRSS.

You are requested to relieve the officer(s) on receipt of confirmation from NATRSS with a
direction to report to NATRSS on 29% April 2013 at 9.30 A.M. sharp.

(This issues with the approval of Director, NATRSS)

Subject: Intra-Regional Transfer within a political state(erstwhile region prior to
bifurcation) on compassionate ground in the cadre of SSA- Regarding
Sir,

This office circular no. HRM-IV/III/14/2/2002/Genl/Pt./1853 dated 29.04.2011
provides for the guidelines on Inter-Regional Transfer of Social Security Assistants on
compassionate grounds. Accordingly, transfer requests on compassionate grounds from SSA
are being forwarded by Regional Offices to Head Office for consideration.

It has been decided that the applications from SSA for transfer on compassionate grounds
within a political state (erstwhile region prior to bifurcation) does not fall in the category of
Inter Regional Transfer as mentioned in the circular dated 29.04.2011.

Therefore, Intra Regional Transfers of SSAs within a political state (erstwhile regions prior
to bifurcation) shall be effected only with the approval of Addl. CPFC of the political states.
However, the request for transfer within the same region (after bifurcation) shall be effected
only with the approval of RPFC Gr. I of the bifurcated region.

However, such transfers shall be subject to the following guidelines:-
(i) His/her Seniority& Pay would not be affected.

(ii) Since the transfer being allowed at his/her own request, he/she will not be entitled to
any TA/DA and Joining time.

(iii) His/her past service rendered in the station prior to his/her such transfer would be
counted for the purpose of appearing in the departmental examination.
-1-

(iv) Intra-Regional Transfer request would be considered on compassionate grounds
depending upon facts and merits of the case subject to administrative exigencies, staff
position/requirement in the Regional/Sub-Regional Office/District Office from where
transfer is sought and vacancy position/requirement in the Regional/Sub-Regional
Office /District Office where transfer is requested.

OFFICE MEMORANDUM
Sub:- Revision of pension of pre-2006 pensioners — reg.

The undersigned is directed to say that in pursuance of Government’s decision
on the recommendations of Sixth Central Pay Commission, orders were issued for
revision of pension/family pension vide this Department’s OM No.38/37/08P&PW(A) dated 1.9.2008, as amended from time to time.

+ The pension/family pension of pre-2006 pensioners was stepped up to 50% of
the sum of minimum of pay in the pay band and the grade pay corresponding to the
pre-revised pay scale from which the pensioner had retired as arrived at with reference
to the fitment tables annexed to the Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure
OM No.1/1/2008-IC dated 30 August, 2008 with effect from 24.9.12 vide this
Department OM of even number dated 28" January, 2013.

3. In regard to disbursement of revised pension/family pension, while Head of
Departments are responsible for sanctioning of pension/family pension, in cases where
revision has already been done by PAOs consequent to 6 CPC, the revision may be
effected at the level of PAOs. A copy of the revised authority may be sent to
HOD/DDO for record. In cases where no revision has been effected, Head of Offices
may follow normal procedure for revision of pension/family pension. Even in cases
where there is no change in pension/family pension as a result of the issue of this OM,
a revised authority for no change may be issued by the PAQs. The finalized authority

will be sent to CPAO for further necessary action.

4, A suitable entry regarding the revised pension/family pension shall be recorded
by the pension Disbursing Authority in both halves of the Pension Payment Order, —

5. In case the pension/family pension in respect of pre-2006 pensioners/family
pensioners has not already been revised w.e.f. 1.1.2006, the same may also be revised
for the period upto 23.9.2012 in terms of order dated 1.9.2008 and subsequent orders
thereto and for the period from 24.9.12 in terms of order of even number dated
28.1.2013.

6. CGA/CPAO/Ministry of Defence/Ministry of Railways/Department of
Posts/Department of Telecom will devise their own monitoring mechanism to ensure

ie that enhanced pension and arrears are disbursed to all civil pensioners/family

IMPORTANT
Subject: Issuance of Multi City Cheques.

Sir,

This is with reference to directions of Reserve Bank of India issued vide circular
No.DPSS.CO.CHD.No.399/04.07.05/2012-13 dated 03.09.2012 regarding compulsory use of
multi-city/payable at par CTS-2010 standard cheques w.e.f. 01.04.2013.

2. In this connection, it has been decided that a full-proof system for payment to the
beneficiaries in respect of A/c No.1 and 10 to be introduced through Multicity cheque Type-29
with CTS-2010 standard under Corporate Cheque Payable At Par (CCPAP) wherever the
payment is not possible through NEFT. Therefore, the following operational exercise have
been suggested by SBI:-

(i) The CCPAP facility will be allowed by SBI in the Existing Account No.1 and 10 of
EPFO and therefore, the Field Offices may take up the matter with link branch for
issuing multi city cheques Type 29. For this purpose the letter No. SME/L&TP/111
dated 10.12.2012(copy enclosed) of CGM(SME), SBI, Corporate Centre, Mumbai
may be quoted to the link branch, if need be.

(ii) The existing stock of general cheques (Non CTS 2010) may first be exhausted/used
by Field Offices followed by MCC Type 29 Cheques. For example, if the existing
stock of general cheques is exhausted on any date before 31.03.2013, you may start
issuing MCC Type 29 cheques even before 01.04.2013.

(iii) Till the CCPAP Module take place, the existing instructions issued vide Head Office
letter No. Bkg/Fraud/05/15614 dated 24.11.2011 (posted at Sr. No. 408 Under
Office Order/Circulars for 2011-12 on Official website of EPFO) are to be followed
for both general cheques as well as MCC Type 29 cheques which would be
containing maximum limit upto Rs.50 lacs. In case of later, the amount may be
restricted suitably till the date of conversion of existing Accounts into CCPAP
Account. Please ensure that the cheque amounts should be within the limit
prescribed for each account in both cases. The payment beyond the prescribed limit
of the amount will continue to be made by issuing draft/bankers cheques at par
without any charges to be paid to SBI. In this connection the letter No.
SME/L&TP/138 dated 22.01.2013 from CGM (SME) SBI, Corporate Centre,
Mumbai may be quoted to the link branch, if need be, whereby the facility of

issuance of draft/bankers cheques free of charge has been extended by SBI upto
30.06.2013.

(iv) Since the other Bank accounts No.2, 21 & 22 are saving bank accounts, the Field
Offices may apply for multi-city/payable at par CTS-2010 standard cheques as per
directions of RBI.

3. In view of above, all Regional/Sub-Regional offices may apply for multi-city
cheques immediately so that the same are made available with the offices by the time existing
stock of cheques is exhausted or the date 01.04.2013 whichever occurs earlier as under: .

e For Account No. 1 & 10 — Apply for multi-city Type 29 with CTS-2010
standard cheques.

e For Account No.2, 21 & 22 — Apply for multi-city/payable at par CTS-2010
standard cheques.

4, Regarding implementation of CCPAP in respect of A/c No. 1 & 10, separate
communication will follow.

The Commission has been emphasising on the need for observing integrity,
transparency, fairness and equity in all aspects of decision mak~ng including in tendering and
award of contracts. However, the Commission is still receiving complaints regarding adoptlon
of non-transparent methods in tendering and award of contracts. A number of such complaints
pertam to award on nomination (single source procurement) basis instead of following a
process of open competitive bidding. The Commission in thelr earlier office order No. 23/7/07
dated 05.07.2007(copy enclosed) had laid down the exceptional circumstances where 'single
source procurement' can be resorted to. These guidelines were consequent to the Supreme
Court's judgement in case of Nagar Nigam, Meerut v/s A1 Faheem Meat Export Pvt. Ltd. [SLP
(Civil) No 1074 of 20061.
2.
In view of the complaints being recerved regarding award of contracts on 'nomrnatlon
basis' without adequate justification, the Commission has decided to reiterate their earlrer
rnstructions for strict implernentat~on. The Commission has also observed that there have been
Instances where government organisationslPSUs obtain contract from other government
organisationslPSUs and further award the same to private entities on 'back to back tie up' bass
without competitrve tendering mechanrsm and w~thout any significant value addition by the
procuring government organisation/PSU. This practice subverts the Comm~ssron's emphasis on
integrity, transparency, fairness and equity in decision making. It is therefore, necessary to
curb this practice. Further, the Comm~ssion directs that details of all tenders awarded on
nomination basis shall be posted on website in public domain as per Commission's office order
of 5'"uly

No. HRM-TIAGHC/1(1)/2013

In order to address the expeditious settlement of rightful grievances related to
service matters of all the officers upto the level of RPFC Gr. I and all other officials, an|
Internal Grievances Handling Committee (IGHC) consisting of following officers has been|
constituted :- ;

1. FA & CAO
2. ACC (Pension)
3. ACC (IS)

Such committee shall consider all the matters except those relating to
transfer/postings. The officers/officials can convey their individual grievances via e-mailrc.hrm@epf.india.gov.in or in writing.

The RPFC (HRM) or the RPFC Gr. I of the branch/section to which the grievance is
related shall present the facts of the case to the meeting of IGHC. However, the IGHC shall
take only such grievances into cognizance that are routed through ACC (HR).

The Committee is directed to hold atleast one meeting every fortnight so that all
the grievances are disposed expeditiously.

Sir,

I, while expressing my gratitute and thanks to you for your past support and coOperation in making similar programmes held earlier a huge success, again solicit your
support for the same.

This Institute is organising a two days special course for Employers and
Employees of exempted/unexempted Estt. from 28/02/13 to 01/03/13. In this programme
various provisions of EPF Act 1952 and Schemes will be discussed in detail, and along
with it, New EPFO Application Softwares will also be discussed. During the launch of new
softwares and implementation of new changes, a greater need has been felt for a detailed
and thorough training programme for employers and employees who are the first stake
holder of this social security organization.

The present training programme intends to put a greater emphasis in addressing
such new changes. You are, therefore, once again requested to nominate your officers to
this training course to enable them function smoothly having full exposure to EPF Act and
Schemes. The fee for this course is Rs. 3,000/- (Rupees Three Thousand Only) per
participant. It includes lodging and boarding charges. Nominations along with Demand
Draft of (fees) Rs.3,000/- per person in the name of RPFC,ZTI(WZ), Ujjain payable at
Ujjain may be sent immediately for an early registration for the training course.

Sub: Notice for agitation for non-settlement of legitimate demands - regarding.

Sir,
The All India EPF Staff Federation has given a notice for agitation for non-settlement
of its legitimate demands.

2. The issues raised by the Federation was placed before the CPFC for consideration and
a point wise reply was given to the Secretary General, AIEPFSF on the action taken and the
status of each of the issues raised by the Federation was informed vide this office letter of
even No. dated 24.01.2013 which is uploaded at EPFO official website.

3. It has been informed to the Staff Federation that there has not been a single issue on
which the EPFO Authorities have been unresponsive. All the issues have been responded and
taken for consideration in an appropriate manner. It has been the endeavour of EPFO to
consider and support all the just and legitimate demands of the Federation without
compromising the larger interest and goal of the organisation. As a result there had been no
occasion for any discord between the EPFO management and the Federation.

4. Keeping in view of the aforesaid, the Federation was requested to call off its agitation
notice and come forward to discuss the issues.

5. Further, the CPFC had a meeting with the Secretary General and some office bearers of
the All India EPF Staff Federation on 25.01.2013. The CPFC heard the office bearers on
various issues raised by them and assured them that all the issues which can be settled at his
level will be looked into for taking appropriate decisions.

6. It is unfortunate that despite the aforesaid, the Staff Federation has continued with its
agitation programme. In this regard, it may be noted that the said act of the Staff Federation
is against the spirit of Rule 7 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 which is mutatis-mutandis
applicable to the officials of EPFO by virtue of EPF (Officer and Employees Conditions of
Service) Regulations, 2008. The Sub-Rule 2 of Rule 7 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules provides
that -

“no govt. servant shall resort to or in any way abet any form of strike or coercion or physical
duress in connection with any matter pertaining to his service or the service of any other
Government servant.

Further, the Govt. vide MHA OM No. 25/23/66-Ests.(A), dated 09.12.1966 clarified that -
‘strike’ means refusal to work or stoppage or slowing down of work by a group of employees
acting in combination, and includes -

(i) mass absentation from work without permission (which is wrongly described as "mass
casual leave");

(ii) refusal to work overtime where such overtime work is necessary in the public interest;

(iii) resort to practices or conduct which is likely to result in, or results in the cessation or
substantial retardation of work in any organization. Such practices would include, what are
called ‘go-slow’, ‘sit-down’, ‘pen-down, stay-in’, sympathetic” or any other similar strike; as
also absence from work for participation in a Bandh or any similar movements.

Government servants who resort to action of the above kind violate rule 7 (ii) of the

Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964 and disciplinary action can be taken against

them.

7.

Therefore the agitation programme in which any of the activities as mentioned in

Para 6 (i) (ii) (iii) is resorted will attract the provisions of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 and
would be in violation of Rule 7 of the said Rules and would make such participating officials
liable for disciplinary action against them.

8.

In view of the above, the Officer In-charge of all the EPFO offices are advised to ensure

punctuality, office decorum and to strict discipline under the rules and ensure proper
functioning in their respective offices and take appropriate action as provided in Rule 7 of the
CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964.

[This issues with the approval of CPFC]

Subject: Leveraging Aadhaar for improving the services of EPFO -
regarding.

Sir,

This is in reference to Head Office letter No. RI/UID/2010/30051 dated
21.01.2013 on the subject cited above.

The issue of expeditious enrolment of the EPF members was discussed
with UIDATI Officials. It has emerged that UIDAI through its registrars has been
organising enrolment camps in 18 states only. Register General of India (RGI)
has been collecting data in respect of the remaining states through National
Population Register (NPR). While the data collected by RGI is also being
processed for issue of Aadhaar numbers by UIDAI, the methodology used by
RGI for setting up enrolment camps is different i.e. it is being done on the
basis of house-to-house data collected by enumerators during Census
Operations 2011, unlike UIDAI camps, where any resident, irrespective of the
place of residence, can get himself enrolled for Aadhaar number. Thus

enrolment may take considerable time.

In view of the discussions held with UIDAI officials and the time required
in the process of obtaining Aadhaar numbers, it may not be possible to obtain

Aadhaar number/ Aadhaar Enrolment number by EPF members by 1* March,

2013. Therefore, it has been decided to not to make Aadhaar
Number/Enrolment number mandatory for EPF members from 1* March, 2013.
However, the field offices would make maximum efforts to obtain the available

Aadhaar numbers of the EPF members.

Further your attention is invited to Head Office letter no. MIS-II/ISO9001/2011-12/24686 dated 9° November 2012 on implementation of ISO
9001 Certification for the field offices which is a mandatory success indicator
under the Results Framework Document (RFD). The updation of members’
master in database is one of the standards required for the purpose. In view of
the benefits that would accrue both to the EPF members as well as EPFO, it has
now been decided to collect the core banking account number of all the

contributing members as indicated in ECR.

The Regional offices and Sub-Regional offices should make an all-out
effort to collect the core banking account numbers in respect of all the
contributing members as indicated in ECR. Compliance of instructions may

kindly be ensured in this regard.

Yours faithfully,

Sub: Formation of Committee on Accounting Procedure.

The Centra! Provident Fund Commissioner has constituted a Committee to
address the following issues: -

a) Evaluate and assess the present accounting system {i.e single entry
system), its limitations and lack of checks and balances.

b) Prescribe such books of accounts, ledgers, journals which should be
maintained by EPFO in order to migrate to double entry accounting
system.

c) Prescribe the flow of information in order to maintain such books of
accounts/fledgers/ournals and also to map the responsibility of
Officials/officers who will either prepare/maintain or supervise the flow of
entries into these books of accounts.

d) Assess the requirement of output in terms of service delivery to the
beneficiary, to the employer and also for the process of compliance to the
EPFO rules and aiso keep such requirement into consideration for
prescribing the books of account/ledgersfournals.

e) Assess the sufficiency of the flow of information coming to Organisation
through various forms/challans etc. for maintaining the prescribed books of
accounts/edgers/oumals also for generating desired output such as claim
settlement and determination of pension.

f) On the basis of above analysis if the committee so desires will also
redesign the forms, challans received either from the employer or
employee or the financial intermediary such as banks, custodians, Fund
Managers etc. while prescribing alteration in the forms or mapping the
responsibility of the officer for preparing, maintaining or supervising the
books of A/c, Ledger or Joumal, care will be taken te suggest only such
changes which are considered essential in order to achieve maximum
business continuity.

g) In the process of making its study and recommendation, the committee will
take into cognizance the prevailing accounting standards and mandatory
accounting norms prescribed for the existing Pension Funds or for related
industry such as mutual fund/insurance etc. in the country.

h) Directive of CAG issued from time to time for maintaining books of
accounts of double entry system is also to be considered.
2. The Committee will comprise of following officers:-
1. Shri Rajesh Bansal, ACC(HR&RJ) - Chairman
2. Shri M. Narayanappa, RPFC-I(iS)HO - Member
3. Shri Abhay Ranjan, RPFC-I (F&A) HO - Member
4. Shri S.K. Suman, RPFC-Il(Vadeckar) - Member
5. Shri Navendu Rai, RPFC-Il(Conf)HO - Member
6. Shri Sanjay Kesar, RPFC-II(NDC) - Member

7. Shri Manoranjan Kumar, RPFC-Il (Invst.)HO- Member

Shri M.S. Arya, RPFC-Il (WSU), Head Office will assist the Committee as
Convener.

3. The Committee may co-opt any other member or direct any other officer in
EPFO to participate /assist in the above task. It is expected that the Committee
will submit its presentation and draft report to FA & CAO within one month for
further discussion and deliberation with the Central P.F. Commissioner.

Sir,
The Central Board of Trustees, in its 157th meeting held on 09.07.2002 had approved
the proposal for allowing Insurance Companies in Private Sector coming under the regulatory
control of IRDA to offer the Group Insurance Scheme conferring similar or better benefits
than the Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme,1976 for the purpose of grant of
exemption from the Employees' Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme,1976.
2.
M/s Star Union Dai-ichi Life Insurance Company Limited,
has approached the
Employees' provident Fund Organisation for approval of the 'Group Term Insurance Plan'
offered by them in lieu of Employees'
Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme,1976.The salient
features of the policy are as under:
(i)
The policy is arranged to provide Assurance benefits to the employees with a
minimum of Rs. 1,32,000/- as the product m' imum is Rs. 1,32,000/-.

(ii) All the
members of the
Employees' Provident Funds Scheme,1952 in the
establishment will be eligible to be members of the policy. The member becomes
eligible for the coverage as soon as he/she becomes the member of the
Employees' Provident Funds Scheme,1952.
(iii) No member shall withdraw
from the
Scheme as long as he satisfies the
conditions of the eligibility described above.
(iv) The employer(policy holder) will give an undertaking to the effect that all new
members have been included from the date of their joining. If a death claim is
received in respect of a member whose premium and/or name is not submitted
to M/s Dai-ichi Life Insurance Company Limited, the employer undertakes to
provide the benefits for the same.
(v) "The
Beneficiary"
shall mean the
person or
persons who
has/have
been
nominated by the Member/s as beneficiary/beneficiaries and will be the same as
envisaged under the Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme,1976.
3.
On a careful examination of the proposal submitted by M/s Star Union Dai-ichi Life
Insurance Company Limited, it has been found that the benefits conferred by their policy are
better than the benefits under the Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme,1976.
Accordingly, it has been decided to enlist M/s Star Union Dai-ichi Life Insurance Company
Limited to provide their 'Group Term Insurance Plan' in lieu of Employees' Deposit-Linkec
Insurance Scheme,1976. Therefore, those employers who opt for this 'Group Term Insurance
Plan' of M/s Star Union Dai-ichi Life Insurance Company Limited to cover their employees
shall be entitled for grant of relaxation/exemption from Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance
Scheme,1976.

Sub: Notice for agitation for non-settlement of legitimate demands -Regarding.

Sir,
Please refer to your letter No. agitation notice/2012/104 dated 09.11.2012 on the subject
cited above.

In this context, the issue has been considered by the CPFC and point wise comments on
the demand raised by the Federation are as under:-

1. (a) Sanction of staff as per SIU norms.

A committee of four Additional CPFC’s was constituted by the CPFC on the issue. The
Committee has submitted its report with its recommendations. The recommendations were
sent to the Finance wing for concurrence. The Finance wing had made some observations on
the proposal which is being replied by the HR wing.

1. (b) Sanction of PA/PS/ Stenographers Post-proportionate to the increase in Group-A posts.

The matter was put up before the EC, CBT and the Executive Committee has made some
observations. A revised proposal is under consideration.

2. Enhancement of fixed Medical allowance to Rs.3500/- due w.e.f. 01.01.2012.

A proposal in this regard is being placed in the ensuing Executive Committee meeting of the
CBT, EPF for consideration.

3. Implementation of Anomaly committee report constituted for the employees/officers of the
organisation after 6th CPC like Grade pay of Rs. 5400/- to EO/AO and Rs. 4800 to Section
Supervisors respectively.

The report on anomaly committee was placed before the EC meeting on 6% Aug., 2010. The
EC decided that a comprehensive proposal for re-structuring of all cadres of EPFO be
prepared and sent to the govt. for consideration. Accordingly, a proposal was sent to the
Govt. on 19.07.2011. The Government vide letter No.A-11013/1/2011-SS-I dated 25.10.2012

EPS

conveyed the observations of the Ministry of Finance on the proposal and requested for a
revised proposal. The same is under process.

. Payment of 6th CPC arrears w.e.f. 01.01.06 instead of 01.09.07 in respect of scales upgraded
on 24.09.2007 by CBT EPFO.

The proposal for preponing the date of arrears was sent to the Government vide HO letter
dated 01.09.2011 and again vide letter dated 09.07.2012. The Government vide letter dated
11.10.2012 conveyed that the request has not been acceded. The same was informed to the
General Secretary of the Federation vide HO letter dated 18.12.2012.

. Continuation of time bound promotion scheme w.e.f. 01.04.2004 to 31.08.2008 as allowed by
the Govt. Pursuance to 6% CPC.

It was decided during the last meeting with the Federation representatives held on
22.05.2012 that the matter may be sent to Govt. Accordingly, the mater was sent to the Govt.
vide letter dated 20.07.2012 for consideration of the case. The MOLE vide its letter dated
27.07.2012 referred the matter back with the request that a self contained note containing
background of the case may be sent. Accordingly a self contained note has been sent to the
Govt. vide letter dated 22.11.2012. The response of the govt. is awaited.

. Enhancing Quota for promotion to the post of APFC from the post of EO/AO/PS/SO i.e. from
50% to 75% & resultant reduction in DR Quota to 25% and reduction of qualifying service for
promotion from 7 years to 4 years.

The matter was discussed in the meeting with the Federation held on 10.04.2012. The
recruitment rules for the post provide a ratio of 50:50 between departmental promotion
quota and direct recruitment. The APFC cadre in EPFO is the entry level Group ‘A’ cadre of the
Organisation and it requires a mix and balance of experience and youth. The ratio between DP
and DR meets that requirement and serving that objective. Therefore the demand of the
Federation for enhancing promotion quota for the post of APFC from 50% to 75% is not
feasible and could not be acceded to.

. Reduction of qualifying service for promotion from the post Section supervisors to the post of
EO/AO on seniority basis from 5 years to 3 years at par with Exam Quota.

The promotional channel for the post of EO/AO is from the feeder cadre of Section Supervisor
(with Grade pay of 4200/-). As per DoP&T instruction dated 24.03.2009 the qualifying service
for the said promotion from GP 4200 to 4600 is 05 (five) years.

. Review of productivity linked Bonus Scheme which is due w.e.f. 01.01.2006.

The MoL&E vide letter dated 18.09.2012 conveyed the approval for payment of PLB for
the year 2011-12. While conveying the approval, it was communicated that Ministry of
Finance has observed that there is uncertainty regarding introduction of Performance Related
Incentive Scheme (PRIS). It would be appropriate that MoL&E start working on a new scheme
of PLB for EPFO.

scheme formulated by the National Productivity Council and recommended by the EC, CBT,
EPF had already been sent to the MoL&E vide letter dated 27.12.2006. Further, in 57%
meeting of the EC, CBT, EPF held on 23.02.2007, it was decided that pending 6" Pay

Reference: H.O. letter No. R-I/UID/2010/Pt/27938 dated 20.12.2012.
Subject:- Leveraging Aadhaar number to improve the services of EPFO.

This is in continuation to earlier letter referred above. It is reiterated that the Aadhar
platform can be leveraged to improve the services of EPFO by using it as Know-Your-Customer
(KYC) credentials of EPF members. It has been decided to make the Aadhaar numbers
mandatory for the new members. However for the existing members, the seeding of Aadhaar

numbers has to be done in a time-bound manner.

To carry out the process of collection of Aadhaar numbers of EPF members the following

action plan has been devised:-

(a) The field offices should contact the local UIDAI authorities requesting them to set up camps

for enrolment in industrial areas and other places, which they find suitable for the purpose.

District authorities may also be contacted if they are organizing camps for such enrolments.

(b) The information may be captured in the format that would be made available along with

the instructions for modalities to capture details in the employer portal on the EPFO

website. Clear instructions should be given to the employers to maintain the information in
the excel format till the facility to capture/upload information on employer portal is made

available.

(c)

(d)

(e)

(f)

As in respect of the new EPF members joining on and after March 1, 2013, the submission
of Aadhaar number would be mandatory, the field offices should inform the employers to
collect the Aadhaar details as above mandatorily in respect of all its new members. In
respect of the members, who have not been issued Aadhaar number, employers should
give the Enrolment ID (EID) which are provided at the time of enrolment. EID would be
converted to Aadhear number later on. The information is to be kept in the format as
explained above till the facility is made available on the employer portal.

The Aadhaar details in respect of pensioners are to be collected directly or through banks.
In this regard, legible copies of Aadhaar letter issued by UIDAI, first page of Pension
Payment Order (PPO) and first page of passbook containing Bank Account No. and IFSC
code. A provision would be given in the system to generate letters as enclosed at Annexure
‘A’ with PPO number, name and address in English, which can be despatched in window
envelope to the pensioners. The local office may print the translation of the letter in
vernacular language on a leaflet and attach it with the letter for better communication.

The publicity for the same should be made by field offices through local newspapers.
Simultaneously, the publicity would be provided through website, SMS and e-mail
(wherever available).

The development of facility to be provided on employer portal for the purpose is under
process and would be provided shortly. Thereafter, the Aadhaar details would be
captured/uploaded in the format provided through Employer portal.

It is, therefore, requested to take necessary action as above to ensure the collection of

data in respect of all new members joining on or after 1° March, 2013 on monthly basis and In
J

respect of existing members by 30" June, 2013.

Sub: Filling up of two posts of Legal Assistant in E.P.F. Organisation, Headquarters in the

Pay Band PB-2 Rs. 9300-34800 with Grade Pay of Rs.4200/- on deputation basis.

Sir,

Two posts of Legal Assistants in the Pay Band PB-2 Rs. 9300-34800 with Grade Pay of
Rs.4200/- are to be filled up by “transfer on deputation” basis in Head Office for a period not
exceeding three years from amongst the existing employees working in Hqrs./ROs/SROs/SAOs/ZOs
& Training Institutions of the Employees Provident Fund Organisation. The requisite qualification is
as under:

Essential :

(a) Degree in Law of a recognised University or equtvalent.

(b) Should hold post in the Pay Band PB-2 Rs.9300-34800with Grade Pay Rs.
4200/- or equivalent on regular basis or should have rendered at least 5 years
regular service in the post in the Pay Band PB-1 Rs. 5200-20200 with Grade
Pay of Rs.2400/-.

Desirable :

Should have atleast 3 years experience in Legal work in the Employees
Provident Fund Organisation/Central Govt. Department or should be a
qualified legal practitioner who has practiced as such for a period of at least 2
years at the Bar.

2. Accordingly, you are requested to arrange to circulate the above vacancies amongst the staff
members of your Regional and Sub-Regional Offices and the applications recetved from the
candidates fulfilling the prescribed requirements as indicated above along with their detailed service
particulars as per enclosed proforma and the photocopies of the Annual Confidential Reports for the
last five years duly attested, may please be forwarded to this office so as to reach this office not later
than 31.01.2013. Maximum age limit of applicant for appointment by deputation is 56 years as
on closing date of receipt of application i.e. 31.01.2013. In case no application is received by the
stipulated time, it will be presumed that there is no applicant for these posts from your region.

Yours Faithfully,

Encl.: As above.

Subject: Updation of Members’ Accounts for the years 201 {-4i2- Regarding.

Sir,

As per data extracted from the website of EPFO as on 21.12.2012, it is observed that 94.13 Lakh
accounts are pending for updation for the year upto 2011-12. This includes the pendency of 7.23 Lakh,
10.06 Lakh and 76.84 Lakh accounts for the year 2009-10, 2010-11 and 2011-12 respectively. Whereas
all the annual accounts for the period upto the year 2011-12 were to be updated by 30" September 2012.

It is observed that few of the offices have already achieved the targets but majority of the offices
are still lagging behind the stated target. The delay in updation of members’ accounts generates a lot of
members’ grievances and at the same time delays the process of settlement of claims.

The issue has been examined at the Head Office and accordingly it has been decided to update all
the members’ accounts for the year upto 2011-12 latest by 31.03.2013. All the RPFCs/Officers-Incharge
are hereby requested to mobilize all the resources and ensure that all the pending accounts are updated by
the target date. In case of any technical problem hindering the updation of accounts, the issue may be
directly taken up with the IS Division for its early solution under intimation to the undersigned.

In this regard, all the Addl. CPFCs of the Zones are also requested to monitor/review the progress
of offices within their zone on regular basis at their level and ensure that the targets are met by the
offices under their jurisdiction.

(Issues with the approval of FA&CAO).
faithfully,

(Abilify Ranjan)

Sub:- SUBMISSION OF ANNUAL IMMOVABLE PROPERTY RETURN FOR THE YEAR
2012 (ENDING 31.12.2012)- BY GROUP ‘A’ OFFICERS-UPLOADING THE SAME
IN PUBLIC DOMAIN-REGARDING.
Sir,
As per Rule 18 (1) (ii) of CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, it is mandatory for all Group *A’
officers to submit their Immovable Property Return in respect of a calendar year by 31°‘ January
of the following year.

The Annual Immovable Property Return (AIPR) for the year 2012 will become due on
1.1.2013. It is requested to advice all Group *A’ officers to submit their AIPR for the year 2012
(as on 1.1.2013) complete in all respect (including full name and dated signature) within the
stipulated time i.e. latest by 31° January 2013 invariably in the format prescribed (annexed
herewith).

It may be ensured that phrases such as “Same as previous year”, “No change” etc. are not
used in the AIPR and full particulars of the Immovable Property inherited/owned/acquired or
held are furnished in all the columns specified in the AIPR in terms of Rule 18 of CCS (Conduct)
Rules, 1964.

As per DoPT’s O.M. No. 11012/112007-Estt.A dated 27.9.2011 and MoLE Circular no.
C-29020/12011-Vig. dated January 2, 2012 (copy enclosed), vigilance clearance shall be denied

(1/4)

to Group ‘A’ officers who do not submit their Annual Immovable Property Return by the
prescribed time limit (in the given format).

Further, appropriate entry regarding late submission/non-submission of AIPRs should be
made in the relevant APARs of the concerned officer in terms of DoPT’s OM dated 11.7.2011
and No. 2101128/93- Estt. (A) dated 20.10.93.

The decisions of Govt. of India in the Circulars/O.M.s cited above and others on the
subject may be brought to the notice of all the officers concerned and they may be requested to
adhere to the time line and format indicated above.

The RPFC-I In-charge of the Region shall consolidate and forward all the AIPRs
alongwith a list of defaulting officers as on 1.2.2013 latest by 8.2.2013. A compliance report on
the above may kindly be forwarded via e-mail to: re.hrm@epfindia.gov.in.

Yours faithfully,

Sub: - Implementation of Direct Cash Transfers under various schemes in
EPFO - Reg.

The schemes of the EPFO involving transfer of benefits to the beneficiaries namely
Pension, withdrawal of Provident Fund, premature withdrawal of Pension, Payment related
to EDLI have been identified by Government for implementation of Direct Cash Transfers
from 1* January, 2013 in 43 pilot districts (list enclosed) and in all districts thereafter.

2. In this regard, it has been decided that embedding of Aadhaar numbers in the bank
account of beneficiaries is considered an effective instrument in the Direct transfer
methodology. Therefore there is an urgent need to seed Aadhaar Numbers in the accounts
of the beneficiaries who receive benefits under various schemes of EPFO. In order to
ensure that seeding of the Aadhaar numbers is completed throughout the country in
specified time frame, the Ministry of Labour & Employment has decided that seeding of
Aadhaar Numbers of the beneficiaries be completed for 43 districts by 31° December,
2012 and for the beneficiaries in the rest of the districts as early as possible.

3; For the purpose, a soft copy of the digitized database seeded with Aadhar number
in respect of EPFO subscribers and pensioners is to be made available to the bank. To
ensure that, the Aadhaar number details and Saving Bank Account No. details would be

..collected from the subscribers in the enclosed format. The message to the employer for

providing the data will be spread through the messages in EPFO official website.

4. In addition to above, the field offices are requested to expedite the collection of
Aadhaar details i.e Name and Aadhaar Number w.r.t the EPF account Number for both
subscribers and pensioners by using camp mode in coordination with the local UIDAI
agencies, District authorities. All the possible sources like employers, banks and individual
pensioners are to be tapped to collect the above.

5. It is requested to give utmost priority to enable seeding of Aadhaar Numbers in the
account of the beneficiaries of the identified districts in your jurisdiction by 31% December,
2012 and thereafter, enable seeding of Aadhaar Numbers for the rest of the beneficiaries
as early as possible.

6. A monthly report on the progress made during the preceding month is to be sent to
the Ministry of Labour & Employment. The first such report may be sent on 1* January,
2013 intimating the seeding of the Aadhaar Numbers in the bank accounts of the
beneficiaries belonging to the aforementioned 43 districts.

Yours faithfully,

Centralized Disbursement of EPS’95 Pension
Process Flow (Draft)

A.Preparatory Activities

1. EPFO offices to complete the updation of gaps (like life certificate, Death/remarriage date,
monthly pension processing, etc.) in pensioner & beneficiary details using respective
functionalities provided in Application Software before cut-off date.

2. Hosted as well as Managed Virtual Sever (firewalled) should be in place with https
connectivity to Bank and EPFO offices using MTNL/BSNL Board band Static IP/MPLS.
Access control & transaction log mechanism should also be integrated to prevent trespassing
by unauthorized sources.

3. Server based Digital Signatures are to be obtained from NIC for each EPFO office.

B.Existing Pensioner Data Migration (Before go-live)

4. A new functionality is to be developed in EPFO Application Software to extract pensioners
data excluding Closed cases as on a cut-off date from RO/SRO Database for a particular
bank (disbursement agency) and generate following files in one go by clicking “Generation“
button (Activity-1 : Generation-EPFO) :

a. Single zipped file.to contain Individual PPOs in PDF file format which would be a
reproduced replica of the original PPOs. (EPFO Report-1)

b. Single delimited text file as per the agreed format containing details of PPO. (EPFO
Report-2) ,

c. Summary report in PDF files for verification by the concerned EPFO office. (EPFO
Report-3)

Once verified for the correctness the concerned EPFO office has to approve by clicking

pproval” button for regeneration of above files with digital signatures & encryptions
(wherever required) for uploading into the central server. (Activity-2 : Approval-EPFO)

Designing of File Format, File naming convention & upload/download schedule will be
finalized in consultation with the Bank.

5. EPFO offices will upload the above files into the central server by clicking “Upload” button
using their login through the Static IP/MPLS connectivity. (Activity-3: Upload-EPFO)

Sub: CAG Report on performance review of the working of
EPFO for the period 2006-2011 - regarding
Sir,
While conducting the performance audit of. EPFO for the period 2006-07 to
2010-11, the CAG has pointed out certain discrepancies which are required to be noted
by all the filed offices for strict adherence so that such obsewatlons are not repeated
In future. An Actlon Taken Report In confirmation to the compliance of this direction
may also be forwarded to Head Office.
2.
The CAG report has pointe,d out that the filed offices do not take prompt
action to collect the fines awarded by the Courts and deposit them In EPF account. The
observations is made on the basis of the date provided by the RO/SROs. All the
RPFCs/OICs of RO/SROs are advised to be careful in monitoring the court cases, their
disposal and prompt collection of fines wherever awarded.
3.
The CAG report has also pointed out that there is considerable delay in filing IPC
cases where the contributions deducted from the wages of the employees are not
remitted to the statutory account by the employer, The Audit noted that the substantial
delay in Initiating appropriate legal proceedings by the EPFO seriously impacts the
timely collection of, dues, The instruction in this regard is once again reiterated that
the concerned assessing officers/officer-in-charge of compliance matter should ensure
filing of police complaints with the police authorities on month to month basis
wherever such offences occur and are detected.
4.
These instructlons are for strict compliance. Please acknowledge recelpt and
forward Action Taken Report.

Sub:-
Approval of Group Term Insurance Plan "Sampoorn Suraksha" issued by
MIs
581 Life Insurance Company Limited for issuance in lieu of the
Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976.
Sir,
The Central Board of Trustees, it its 15ih
meeting had approved the proposal for
allowing Insurance Companies in Private Sector coming under the regulatory control of IRDA to
offer the Group Insurance Scheme conferring similar or better benefits than the Employees'
Deposit Linked-Insurance
Scheme, 1976 for the purpose of grant of exemption from the
Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976.
2.
M/s SBI Life Insurance Company Limited, has approached the Employees' Provident
Fund Organisation for approval of the Group Term Insurance
Plan "Sampoorn
Suraksha"
offered by them for issuance in lieu of Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976.
The salient features of the policy are as under:-
(i)
The Policy is arranged to provide Assurance benefits to the employees with a minimum
of Rs. 1,32,000 as the product minimum is Rs. 1,32,000.
(ii)
All members of the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 in the company will be
eligible to be members of the policy. The member becomes eligible for the coverage as
soon as he/she becomes the member of the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 1952.

Sub: Promotion of Lower Division Clerk who have qualified in
Computer Skill Test for the post of Social Security Assistant
under departmental promotion quota— Regarding

Sir,

Reference have been received from Regional P. F. Commissioner, Andhra
Pradesh and Tamil Nadu seeking clarification as to whether the Lower Division Clerk
who are otherwise fulfilling the eligibility criteria for promotion to the post of Social
Security Assistant under departmental promotion quota can be promoted to the post
of Social Security Assistant on regular/ adhoc basis against an excess operation
under departmental promotion quota but wel! within the total sanctioned strength of
Social Security Assistant.

Consequent upon restructuring the clerical cadre, a new cadre of Social
Security Assistant was introduced in Employee's P. F. Organisation and Recruitment
Rules of said cadre was notified on 3 January 2004. According to notified
Recruitment Rules of said post 85% direct recruitment by open competitive
examination by Employee's P. F. Organisation through an agency or agencies
approved by the CBT/ Transfer failing which by departmental qualifying examination/
Skill Test and 15% by promotion through departmental qualifying examination/ skill
test.

While notifying the Recruitment Rules of Social Security Assistant in the scale
of 4000-6000 (pre-revised) the cadre strength of Social Security Assistant was
reckoned by merging the post of Lower Division Clerk and Upper Division Clerk plus
newly created posts of Social Security Assistant and subtracting there from 576
posts allowed to be retained in the cadre of Lower Division Clerk for promotion from
Group ‘D’ cadres. Al! Upper Division Clerk (regular/adhoc) who were holding the post
at the time of notifying the Recruitment Rules of Social Security Assistant were redesignated as Social Security Assistant w.e.f. 03.01.2004. |

Your attention is invited to Head Office circular no.HRMI11/1(1)2004/SSA/Pt./70077, dated 18.11.2005 and subsequent clarification issued by
Head Office letter of even no. dated 26.09.2008. It is very clear from above said
circulars that all the Lower Division Clerks who were holding the post at the time of
notifying Recruitment Rules of Social Security Assistant and declared successful in
skill test under one time relaxation and subsequently given one more opportunity
should be promoted to the post of Social Security Assistant against the total

sanctioned strength of Social Security Assistant in respective region and they may
be promoted without having regard to Direct Recruitment or Department Promotion
quota.

lt is observed that these guidelines are not followed in proper manner and
vacancy determined in Department Promotion quota are not inconformity with the
instructions/ circular issued by Head Office circulars under reference above and
resultantly some regions have shown 15% departmental examination quota are in
excess.

it is hereby clarified that as far as the Lower Division Clerks who promoted on
or after 03.01.2004 (i.e. the date of notification of Recruitment Rules of Social
Security Assistant) having qualification of Matriculation and above & having 5 years
regular service in the grade are concerned, they can be promoted to the post of
Social Security Assistant against 15% Department Promotion quota subject to
availability of vacancy and on passing of computer skill test of at least 5000 key
depression per hour in data entry.

The contents of circular referred to above are again reiterated for strict
adherence.

Yours faithfully,

Compliance (Administration) shall be forwarded to the Compliance (Judicial) branch for initiation
of an enquiry under section 7A of the Act by the AssessingOfficer.
f)
Before recommending
any case, the
Compliance (Administration)
shall specifically verify,
whether .any report/record
is available on the file indicating the status of the establishment, i.e.
whether it is a closed establishment etc.
g)
Complete investigation
report should be available on record before initiation
of inquiry is
recommended by the Compliance (Administration).
In cases where the complete report is not
received the Compliance (Administration)
shall record reasons in writing
for initiating
the
proposal for the said enquiry.
h)
Except under abnormal circumstances, no inquiry shall be initiated unless a prima-facie case
exists on the basisof the said report.
i)
The AssessingOfficers shall, on receipt of the report from Compliance (Administration) open a
separate file for conducting the quasi-judicial enquiry. This file shall start with the issue of
summons for conducting enquiry under section 7A. The enquiry shall be deemed to have
initiated only if proof of service of notice is available on record.
j)
The 7A notice shall be accompanied by the documents on the basis of which an enquiry is
proposed to be conducted. A copy of draft notice is attached (Annexure A) for reference.
k)
The 7A summons shall be for a specific period i.e. the notice shall not be an open ended notice
and a specific period of default should be compulsorily mentioned in the notice.
I)
It should be compulsorily ensured that the notice has been served on the establishment against
whom an enquiry is proposed to be initiated before any further action is initiated for conducting
a formal enquiry.
m)
If during pendency of 7A enquiry further default is noticed, either another summon be issued to
the establishment for extending the period of current 7A enquiry or a fresh 7A enquiry be
initiated ..

10-14 December, 2012 — Nomination(s) Regarding.

Sir,

The National Academy for Training and Research in Social Security (NATRSS) is conducting a five days
Outbound Training Programme on Team Building & Crisis Management scheduled from 10-14 December
2012 which shall be conducted on 10 & 14" December 2012 at NATRSS and on 11™ to 13" December at
Nadiya Padao Resort, near Jim Corbett National Park.

This Outbound training programme aims at team building from the leadership perspective and to
underline the importance of individual in team building. The main objective of the course is to make the
individual aware of dynamics and constants of team building in varied work situations and to enable the
participants to achieve the common task.

All Additional CPFCs are also requested to participate in the above mentioned programme or
requested to nominate one RPFC-I/RPFC-II level fromm your region including SROs for this programme.

The accommodation in the hostel will be available from one day before the commencement of the
programme till one day after the completion of the training programme. Any extension beyond this will
require specific approval of Director, NATRSS

After receiving the nominations NATRSS will decide the final list of the participants for the above
mentioned programme. You are requested to relieve the officers on receipt of confirmation from NATRSS

The name of the nominated officer may please be communicated latest by 03 December 2012.

(This issues with the approval of Director, NATRSS)

Yours faithfully,

Sub: Implementation of Para10(2) of EPS, 1995- Criteria for deciding eligibility.

Sir,

Now a days a number of representations are being received from Employees’ Pension
Scheme members/Pensioners, demanding 2 years bonus on the basis of ‘eligible service’ i.e. “past
Service + Pensionable Service”/Actual Service).

While some of the offices have been successfully convincing such Employees Pension
Scheme members/ pensioners about the facts that 2 years bonus is admissible only in case of
completion of 20 years of pensionable service i.e. contributory service under Employees Pension
Scheme 1995, others offices at times have not defended the scheme provision with full
justification .

Accordingly, it is requested that such representation shall be disposed off appropriately at
your level as follows —

(1) 2 years weightage will be admissible only after completion of 58 years and 20 years
pensionable service under Employees Pension Scheme 1995 i.e.weightage is due, to be
given only in the year 2015 (November) onwards in such cases.

(2) As past service is not pensionable service, therefore, unless one has completed 20 years
pensionable service 2 years bonus cannot be given.

(3) ‘Past service’ i.e. contributory service under EFPS 71 prior to 16-11-95, when contribution
rate was only 1.16% +1.16%+1.16% is totally different than ‘Pensionable Service’ i.e.
contributory service under EPS 95 after 16-11-95 when contribution rate is 8.33% + 1.16%.
As benefits cannot be same for different contributory rates, therefore the provisions of EPS
95 specifically provide different benefits for past service and pensionable service

Contd...

-2-

(4)

The ‘Past service’ and ‘Actual service’ is added only to decide eligibility for
pension and EPS 95 explicitly provides for the same.

The above guidelines shall be used suitably & selectively depending upon the
exact representation made by the EPS member / pensioner.

Important
Further, please also find enclosed copy of a reply written by RPFC,
Chikmagalur in respect of one such representation. The copy of order of the

DCDRF, Chikmagalur is also enclosed which may please be used in such cases.

36012/45/2005-Estt.(Res.) dated 10.08.2010 regarding “Treating of SC/ST

1995, its work procedures and benefits delivery.

. Describe and evaluate the various provisions of the EPS' 95.

. Create Awareness about Pension scenario in India.

. Clarify doubts regarding benefits under EPS' 95.

. Describe the features of Micro Pension Schemes.

. Describe the role on the Indian pension landscape and its salient features of Different

the programme till one day after the completion of the training programme. Any extension beyond

direction to report to NATRSS on 05.12.2012 at 9.30 A.M. sharp.

Central Vigilance
Commission
being the apex integrity institution of country. has
been striving
to promote
integrity
in various Central
Government
offices
and public
sector undertakings.
Observance
of Vigilance Awareness
Week every year is a step
towards this direction
by the Commission
whereby all the stake holders are enthused
to fight corruption.
2.
The Commission
has decided
that this year the Vigilance
Awareness
Week
would be observed from 29th October (Monday) to 3rd November (Saturday) 2012. The
observance of the Vigilance Awareness
Week should commence with the pledge (copy
enclosed)

Substantive
part
of activities
of a number
of public
organizations
includes
procurement
of goods,
works
and other
services.
Integrity
in public
procurement,
therefore,
is a priority
area in any anti-corruption
strategy.
The risk of corruption
in
public procurement
is dependent
on various
factors
like cost
of the procurement,
complexity of the technology
involved, the urgency to acquire the goods or immediacy
of the project
and the extent
of discretion
enjoyed
by the procurement
officials. A
sound
procurement
system
should
be
able
to
address
these
risk
factors.
For
emphasising
transparency,
accountability
and
probity
in
public
procurement,
the
Commission is committed
to raise awareness.
4.
Apart from creating awareness,
the Commission
expects public organizations to
introduce
e-procurement,
e-payment
etc.
by
leveraging
technology
and
make
measurable
progress in the days ahead in this regard.
The Commission
emphasizes
the public officials to act with integrity, without any fear or favour. Wherever
there is a
knowledge
gap
with
regard
to public
procurement;
measures
for
proper
capacity
building should be undertaken.

Subject: Updation of Members’ Accounts for the years prior to 2011-12 — Regarding.
Sir,

As per data extracted from the website of EPFO as on 17.10.2012, it is observed that 1.68 Crores
accounts are still pending for updation for the year upto 2011-12. Whereas all the annual accounts for the
period prior to 2011-12 have to be updated by 30" September 2012. Some of the offices have already
updated all the Members’ accounts for and upto the year 2011-12 but most of the offices are far behind
the target. All the offices which are lagging behind the target, are required to pay immediate attention on
the issue and ensure that the pendency is cleared at the earliest. It may not be out of context to mention
that this process will expedite the process of claim settlement as well.

In order to improve the progress of updation of members’ accounts at field office level, following
categories of accounts to be attended:

1) Wherever the Form 3A & 6A have already been fed in the system and the updation process is in
pipeline, the same may be expedited.

2) Wherever the Form 3A & 6A and the corresponding contributions have been received but the
process of updation of members’ accounts has not been initiated.

In this regard, all the Addl. CPFCs of the Zones are requested to monitor/review the progress of
offices within their zone in this area, particularly in respect of the above categories of establishments on
weekly basis at their level and forward a copy of the review report to the Head Office. This is also to
mention that this task should be carried out as a ‘Special Drive’ and to be completed within two months.

(Issues with the approval of FA&CAO).
faithfully,

Sub: Declaration of Productivity Linked Bonus (P.L. B.) for the year 2011-2012.
Sir,

The Central Government under Section 5D(7) of the Employees’ Provident Funds &
Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 has conveyed their concurrence for approval! to the extension
of the existing Productivity Linked Bonus Scheme 1998-2004 (Revised) for the year 20) 1-2012
vide their letter No. A-26022/1/94-S.S_I (Part) dated 18.10.2012.

2. Accordingly, the Central Provident Fund Commissioner has been pleased to approve the
payment of the Productivity Linked Bonus, subject to verification of figures relating to workload
and staff in position in each office by the Internal Audit during next audit of Regional Office to the
eligible officials of your Region as per the Productivity Linked Bonus Scheme 1998-2004 for the
year 2011-2012 for 60(Sixty) days in all the offices of EPFO. As per the past practice the
payment of bonus is to be released well before Puja Festival to all Group ‘C’, ‘D’ and Group ‘B’
(Non-Gazetted) employees.

3. The terms and conditions governing payment of P.L.B. will be as per the instructions
issued by the Government of India for payment of the bonus to the employees in Central
Government departments from time to time. However, the quantum of bonus may be assessed as
per the following formula circulated vide Govt. of India, Ministry of Finance O.M. No. 14(1)
E.Co-ord.1/2004 dated 30.9.2004.

= AVERAGE EMOLUMENTS X NUMBER OF DAYS OF BONUS
30.4 (AVERAGE NUMBER OF DAYS IN A MONTH)

4 The Government of India, Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure has already
revised and raised the calculation ceiling to Rs. 3,500/- per month vide OM No. 7(23)/E-III-
‘A/2007 dated 10.10.2008. Hence, all Group C, D, and Group ‘B’ non-gazetted employees are
eligible for bonus. The maximum amount will, however, be restricted to the amount admissible to
those drawing emoluments of Rs.3,500/- per month. The bonus in respect of the employees
drawing emoluments of more than Rs.3,500/- per month will be calculated as if the emoluments
were Rs.3,500/- per month.

5.

The term ‘emoluments’ occurring in these orders wil] include Basic Pay, Personal Pay,

Special Pay, Deputation (Duty) Allowance and Dearness Allowance, but will not include other
Allowances, such as HRA, CCA Special Compensatory (Remote locality) Allowance, Bad
Climate Allowance, Children Education Allowance and Interim Relief etc.

6.

The expenditure incurred for payment of bonus may please be debited in the budget head

“Productivity Linked Bonus.” Payment of Bonus may please be made at the earliest.

7.

The number of employees category-wise who are paid bonus and the total amount

disbursed in each category viz. Group ‘B’ Non-gazetted ‘C’, “D’ may please be intimated to this

Subject: Amendment in Form-11 for identification of Indian International

Sir,

As you are aware an Indian employee having worked or going to work in
foreign country with which India has entered into Social Security Agreement and being
eligible to avail benefits under Social Security programme of that country by virtue of
eligibility gained or going to gain under the agreement is to be treated as International
Worker and contribution, membership to the fund etc in respect of such person will be
regulated by special provisions contained in Para 83 of EPF Scheme, 1952 scheme
1952 and Para 43-A of EPS,1995.

2. Accordingly with a view to identify such Indian Workers who fall under the
category of International Workers, Form 11 (i.e. declaration by the person taking up
employment as stipulated under Para 34 of EPF Scheme, 1952 scheme & Para 24
under EPS, 1995) has been revised with the approval of CPFC and the same is
required to be used by all henceforth.

Yours faithfully,

Subject: National Workshop for Representatives of Exempted Establishments on

29-30 October 2012 — Inviting Nominations - Regarding.
Sir,

The National Academy for Training & Research in Social Security has been conducting National
Workshops for the Exempted Establishment under Employees’ Provident Fund and Miscellaneous
Provisions Act, 1952 for the last several years. Your involvement in collecting the nominations from the
establishments has been very supportive in making the programme a success. Many participants felt that
there should be more such programmes every year as the contents of the programme were really educative
for them to accomplish the tasks before them in administering the fund.

As per the requests of the participants in the earlier programs, and keeping in view the
developments in EPF and EPS Administration, we have designed a two day National Workshop on 29"
and 30" October 2012.

We propose to take up all relevant issues like:

" Provisions of the Act and the Schemes

* Compliance management of exemption

» Nature and periodicity of returns from exempted establishments

« Processes and procedures for better coordination and cooperation

« Investment pattern for provident funds.

* Role of Employers for International Workers under the EPF&MP Act, 1952

A copy of programme announcement and nomination form is enclosed.

You are, requested to collect 4-6 nominations from your region for this programme.

Keeping in view the requirement of exempted establishments and their interest to participate in the
programme, we have kept the participation fee for residential participants @ Rs.8,000/- per participants
covering boarding and lodging, course material etc. and Rs.6,000/- per participant for those who do
not wish to avail accommodation at NATRSS. Stay arrangements will be available for
residential participants in the campus of the Academy from the evening of previous day
i.e. 28.10.2012 and till next day of conclusion of the programme. .

The demand draft drawn in favour of National Academy for Training & Research in Social
Security payable at New Delhi towards participation fee may be sent to the Academy preferably before
15 October 2012. For any further clarification or query you may contact the undersigned at phone
No.011-28521199/26525724, or e-mail: natrss@hetmail.com.

(This issues with the approval of the Director, NATRSS).
Yours faithfully,

( Amit Vashist )}

Sub: Submission of Revised Estimates for the year 2012-13 and Budget Estimates
for the year 2013-14 in respect of Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme, 1952
(including Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995) and Employees’ Deposit
Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976.

In accordance with the provisions regarding budget contained in Para 58
of the EPF Scheme 1952, on probable Receipts and Expenditure relating to the
Administration of the Funds, the Revised Estimates for the year 2012-13 and the
Budget Estimates for the year 2013-14 of the EPF Organisation, based on the
actual Income & Expenditure upto 30 September 2012 (i.e. from 1.4.2012 to
30.9.2012), are to be prepared and placed before the Ceniral Board of Trustees,

for the consideration and approval in this financial year.

2. The budgetary exercise should not be treated as mere routine and if should
receive the personal attention of the Regional Commissioner and the OIC of SRO
for its correctness and fimely submission. On the part of the RPFC (F&A), it snould
be treated as a vital function for the respective Region including for the SROs and
he should devote his personal attention in assisting the Regional Commissioner incharge of the Region. Efforts should be made fo frame the Revised Estimates for
2012-13 in such a manner that there may not be any necessity for Reappropriation/ Additional Funds in the last months of the financial year.

3. The NATRSS Is treated as an independent unit and separate funds are
allotted to meet its own expenditure and the Zonal Training Institutes (ZTls}, Sub-2T!
(Shillong) working under them. As such, Director, NATRSS, will submit Budget
Proposal separately for NATRSS and ZTls including Sub-ZT! (Shillong). Budget for
Deputy Director, Vigilance (NZ) may be included in the proposal of NATRSS.

4. RPFC (ASD), Head Office is also required to submit the proposal of Revised
Estimate 2012-13 & Budget Estimates 2013-14 in respect of Head Office including
the proposal of National Data Centre, Bhavishya Nidhi Enclave and Bhavishya
Nidhi Bhawan regarding requirement of funds under the budget head "Petty
Works & Maintenance of Office Building and Staff Quarters “which wil! be at the
disposal of Chief Engineer, PFD, Head Office.

5. Similarly, the EPF Appellate Tribunal has also been treated as a separate
unit and separate funds are to be allotted fo meet its own expenditure. As such,

Registrar, EPF Appellate Tribunal will also submit budget proposal separately.

6. The following guidelines may please be kepi in mind while formulating the
Revised Estimates for 2012-13 and Budge? Estimates for 2013-1 4: -

(i) One single proposal is required to be prepared in respect of a Region as a
whole py consolidating the proposals of Regional Office and the SubRegional Offices. RPFC-In-Charge of the Region as well as RPFC-II{F&A)}
may therefore get in touch with the OlCs of Sub-Regional! Offices Under
their control immediately to ensure that there is no delay in transmission of
the requisite information to their office. The Revised Estimates for 2012-13
and Budget Estimates for 2013-14 for the offices of Addl. CPFCs (Political
States} and Permanent Inquiry Officers, Zonal Audit Parties and Deputy
Directorates (Vigilance) may include their new requirements, if any, other
then the routine items like Pay & allowances, TA, Stationary, Phone, Fax bills
etc. to the Regional Offices or NATRSS whichever is concerned, where
these offices are situated, which in turn, will include the same in the

consolidated budget proposal of the Region.

(ii) For enable us to assess the amount of coniributions estimated as
receivable during the year 2012-13 (Revised Estimates) and in 2013-14
(Budget Estimates), the details of contributions may be given in Statements
as prescribed in Annexure — BT/A. The figures of Income, Contribution and
Expenditure should be in Rupees format. if there is huge variation the

justification should be indicate.

. There should be a minimum gap of 3- 4 feet between the candidates to ensure that the

answer sheets of one candidate is not visible to the other candidates sitting around them.
There should be one invigilator allotted for every 20 candidates.

The allotment of Invigilator should be roll number wise and changed for each day of the
examination. The details are to be forwarded to this office in the prescribed format (
Annexure ‘III’) for record purpose alongwith the Annexure A-F & Answer Sheets.

. For Examination Centers having more than 60 candidates, invigilators should be called

from outside office i.e. Group ‘A/B’ officers from ESIC, Income Tax, Customs and Excise
etc so that the ratio of invigilators from EPFO and outside should be 2:1. This ratio will be
maintained in addition to the representative from outside office who is a member of the
Board of Examination.

The Invigilators should be handed over the instructions well in advance and a meeting is to
be conducted by the Supervisor (Board of Examination) to inform all the invigilators about
their duties and responsibilities in the examination hall and the strict compliance of the
instructions issued,

The answer sheets after the completion of the examination should be collected by the
Invigilators from those candidates whose roll numbers have been allotted to them and no
one else.

Before collecting the Answer Sheets the Invigilators should verify the following :-

The candidate has written the roll number, paper number, subject, no of continuation sheets
ete correctly.

. All the blank sheets and empty spaces between answers are crossed out by the candidates

completely.

. Candidate has attached all relevant material, supplementary sheets etc with the answer sheet

and tied it securely.

. Ensure that the candidate has not written anything in the question paper and if anything is

found written on it, the same is to be taken from candidate and forwarded to this office
alongwith the report of Supervisor.

. Any candidate found leaving the seat or talking or trying to look into the other candidates:

papers etc , even after the last bell should be immediately reported to the Supervisor.

. No candidates is to be allowed to talk, leave their seats or move till the answer sheets of all

the candidates is collected by the invigilators, counted and accounted for and only then
candidates should be allowed to leave the examination hall.

. Any candidate found with pen in his/her hand after the last bell shall be immediately

reported to the Supervisor and recorded in the report to HQ.

. Supervisor ( Board of Examination) should ensure that all Invigilators have read and

understood all the “Instructions for Invigilators” as circulated vide letter no. Exam/
21(1)2012/ 552 dated 16.03.2012 and also the above instructions.

. No candidate shall be allowed to carry Cell Phones or any electronic devices such as blue

tooth etc. in the Examination Hall.
