Sub: Instructions regarding Computerization Project - reg.

Sir,
CAG, during performance audit of EPFO has pointed out some deficiencies in the
operational aspect of application software. The mentioned aspects have been detailed/clarified
earlier a number of times during trainings/workshops held in regard to the implementation of
computerization project. It is once again reiterated that:-

(a) No password should be reset by the System Admin role until there is a written
request from the user to reset the same. Record of requests should be
maintained in a separate folder for future reference.

(b) The detail of transfer of any user within or out of the office should be recorded in
the system so that the user is permitted to do only those roles for which he is
eligible as per the orders from the administration. The application provides the
facility to record the end date for a task holder in advance in the system and in
such case the privileges are auto barred from such date. Thus in case of
superannuation, the dates can be entered in advance. Moreover, in cases of
transfer, before release of the relieving order physically, the date of relieving can
be entered in the system and then the user will be barred from the privilege
from the date of the relieving.

(c) The role mapping for a user should be done carefully. Only the authorized
persons should be assigned the specified roles in the system. Sufficient
precaution should be taken to ensure that same person should not be assigned
multiple roles in the system which he is not authorized to do simultaneously as
per the Manual of Accounting Procedure. In case of extreme requirements where
it has be done due to administrative exigencies, the officer-in-charge should take
appropriate decision for mapping of roles in such cases.

(d) Release the establishment master and the member balance in all cases. Where
there is some data not to be released for certain reasons, that can be analysed
by the respective Officer-in charge & kept on record for future reference.

Yours faithfully

Pautat-A,

(B.K. Panda)
Addl. Central Commissioner (IS)

Subject: - Furnishing of details required for Assessment and fimely declaration of
Productivity Linked Bonus for the year 2011-12.
Str,

The work relating to the assessment of P.L. Bonus for the year 2011-12 has
been taken up. The revision of PLB Scheme and approval of New Bonus
Scheme is pending with Government, and it may likely to take some more time
for formal approval after the receipt of instructions in this regard from the
Ministry of Finance in the light of recommendations of the 6'* Central Pay
Commission. Hence, it has been decided to collect the information from alll
Regions relating to assessment of P.L. Bonus with reference to existing the P.L.B.
Scheme as approved by Government of India in December, 1999. Information
relating to parameters and performance as per the Scheme is to be furnished,
as usual, in the Annexure A to C (Forms enclosed}.

ACCOUNTS & CASH

2. A time-limit of 30 days {calendar days} has been prescribed for
completing the job relating to setilement of PF, EPS and EDLI claims, Transfer
cases and cases pertaining to Advances. In case the job is not completed
within 30 days, weightage would be reduced to half for the work done beyond
30 days. Date of receipt of claim form {complete in all respect) and the date of
dispatch of cheque/transfer through NEFT would be taken into account for
reckoning 30 calendar days. In some of the cases it was found that the date
mentioned on the cheque is taken into account, which is not correct. The
actual dispatch of cheque takes much more time after the cheque is prepared
and signed by the authorized officer. In order to avoid delay in dispatch it has
been decided that only the actual date of dispatch of cheque as recorded on
the slip issued by the post office should only be taken into account. In other
cases where no cheque is to be issued like PPO, Transfer out not involving
actual transfer of PF accumulations etc., the actual date of issue of PPO and
the date of actual transfer will be taken into account.

3. As regards issue of “Annual Statement of Accounts”, it has been classified
into two groups, Viz. (1} current year’s Accounts slips issued and (2) Previous
year's Accounts slips issued during the current year. Accounts slips relating to
the “current Year" and those pertaining to previous years but issued during the
current year should be shown separately. The Number of accounts slips issued
with the help of outside agencies and the number of accounts slips prepared
and issued on computers of EPFO may also please be furnished separately in
Column 9 of Annexure “A”.

4. Activity “issue of cheque against the PPO of Monthly Pension cases” has
been added in the Bonus scheme, 1999. Those beneficiaries who opt to get
Monthly Pension through their Bank Accounts are sent cheques from the
Regional/Sub-Regional Offices itself. This activity has been included in the PLB
Scheme, 1999 with a view to encourage the staff members fo issue the
cheques of Monthly Pensions as promptly as possible. Accordingly, information
may be furnished separately for all the three categories as provided in
Annexure-A.

ENFORCEMENT & DAMAGES
5. The activities of “Enforcement & Damages” include:

(1} No. of 7A notices issued.
(2) No. of Speaking Orders of 7A passed and compliance effected.
(3) No. of Speaking Orders passed for Levy of Damages.
(4) No.of Recovery Certificates Executed:-
(a} For default in all the five Accounts {A/c No. 1,2,10,21 & 22]

(b) For default in 3 or 4 of the five Accounts.
(c) For default in 1 or 2 of the five Accounts.
7-A NOTICES
6. Only one notice has to be taken into account for all the three Schemes.

In case three separate notices are issued for the three Schemes, it has to be
taken as one only. Further, only the initial notice issued has to be taken into
account and not the notices issued every time after adjournment of
proceedings due to any reason. With the amendment of Section 7A, the RPFCs
are required to decide not only the quantum of dues but also to decide the
Applicability. In such cases also if more than one notices are issued, it should be
taken as one only for the purpose of PLB return.

SPEAKING ORDERS OF 7A PASSED AND COMPLIANCE EFFECTED

7. Against this item all the speaking orders passed under Section 7A should
not be shown. Only those orders passed, which have been complied with,
should be shown. However, instructions contained in the preceding para as “7A
Notices" should also be kept in view.

Reference:- Letter No. Exam.5(1)2011/273 dated 12.07.2012

Sir/Madam,

With reference to above, after examining the final list of candidates received from the
Regions, it is observed that only few regions have mentioned the Provisional Status against the names of
those candidates who are Inter Regional Transferees and who have not completed required service as per
Recruitment Rules in the present region but have completed required service by combining the service
rendered in old and present regions. It is re-iterated that candidature of such candidates shall be
provisional and subject to outcome of the case pending before Hon’ble Supreme Court of India vide SLP No.
30141/2011 & 30142/2011 as intimated in the Notification issued vide Circular dated 12.07.2012 (Circular
No. 222 of website).

Therefore, all Regional P.F. Commissioners — |, In-charge of Regions are requested to
mention the provisional status of candidates as above and forward the revised EXCEL list to Head Office
within two days by e-mail without fail. In case no such cases are present in the Region, a Certificate to
this extent may kindly be forwarded by e-mail clearly mentioning as under :- :

“This is to certify that all candidates of this region have completed the required service in this Region
itself and no provisional candidates are present in this regard”.

Sir,

It is observed from the final list of candidates sent by the Regions, that many of the
Regions have included the name of Data Processing Assistant (DPAs) in the final list of eligible candidates
while some Regions have requested to clarify that whether the DPA cadre is eligible for appearing in the
above said examination . The matter of eligibility of DPA is examined with HRD Division of Head Office and
it is clarified that as per the existing Recruitment Rules for the post of Enforcement Officer /Accounts
Officer the Limited Departmental Competitive Examination Quota (25%) provides amongst the following:-

“Section Supervisors and Junior Hindi Translators with 3 years regular service in the pay
scale of Rs.5000-8000 and DEOs (Gr.C) with three years regular service in the pay scale of Rs.5000-8000
including those DEOs(Gr.C) who have already put in 5 years regular service in DEO(Gr.A) and Social
Security Assistants / Assistants /Stenographers/DEO Gr.‘A’ and Gr.’B’ with 5 years regular service in the
scale of Rs.4000-6000 in the respective region”

As regards, the eligibility criteria for DPA is concerned, the same is not eligible for
appearing in the Limited Departmental Competitive Examination of EO/AO. Similarly, EDP Supervisors and
Assistant Programmers are not eligible for appearing in this examination. Accordingly, the candidature of
such candidates stand cancelled. You are requested to inform the same to the concerned candidates. An
action taken report may be forwarded to this office by 04.09.2012.

Subject: Clarification in respect of International Workers (IWs) - refund / readjustment of
excess amount in pension fund.

Sir,

Consequent upon inclusion of special provisions in respect of International
Workers (Ws) and signing of Social Security Agreements (SSAs) with a number of countries
by the Government of India, the benefit of “detachment” is being availed by the posted
Indian employees by obtaining a Certificate of Coverage (COC) on the basis of which they
are exempted from making contributions in other country up to a certain period. The status
in respect of such employees has been clarified vide Head Office letter No. WWU/7(17)2009
dated 25.05.2012, according to which the persons going on posting with COC will not be
International Workers.

2. In this context, a reference has been received in Head Office wherein it has been
mentioned that in accordance with GSR 148 dated 3.9.2010 (notified in Gazette dated
11.09.2010), the employer has remitted the pension contribution in respect of all
international workers on their enhanced salary with effect from the date of their posting or
notification whichever is later assuming that such workers are IVs. However, in view of
clarification given in letter dated 25.05.2012 as the persons going on posting with COC are
not to be treated as |IVWs, pension contribution in respect of such employees should be
limited to the wage ceiling of Rs.6500/- subject to proviso of para 11(3) of EPS 95 i.e.
voluntary higher contribution on the option of employer and employee.

3. The matter has been considered and it has been observed that as the Indian

employees going on posting with COC do not fall under purview of the IW, contribution in

respect of such employees would be governed by normal provisions. Further, pension
contribution remitted to the pension fund account in respect of such employees, who
have contributed on full salary due to misunderstanding, needs to be re-adjusted by limiting
the contribution in pension fund to wage ceiling of Rs.6500/- and by diverting the excess
amount to the provident fund account of the member.

4, In view of above, it has been decided that ifa request for readjustment of excess
amount from pension fund to provident fund is made by an employer for the reason stated
above, same may be accepted.

This issues with the approval of CPFC.

Sub : Non requirement of outsourced technical manpower from UTIITSL-Reg

Sir,

As you aware of that the outsourced technical manpower through M/s UTIITSL had
been provided to the field offices for implementation and sustained support of the
“Computerisation Project” keeping in view of the shortage of Technical Manpower in EPFO.
The deployment of Technical Manpower through M/s UTIITSL has been approved by the
Executive Committee in its 69'" Meeting held on 8" December, 2010 for a period of 12
months keeping in view that the internal manpower will be recruited.

As per the phased implementation plan (“GO Live”), M/s UTIITSL has been directed
to deploy the manpower in two phases (June and August 2011). Accordingly, the validity of
the agreement has been regularized in the initial deployment period of 12 months i.e. upto
11 August, 2012.

As planned, till now, the required in house (EPFO) technical manpower were not yet
recruited (167 posts are vacant) and hence it is felt necessary to have an assessment of the
outsourced technical manpower to continue the support in the field offices for smooth
operation of the systems and to support the technical staff for the day to activities (user
support, daily backups, upload / download of data, generating reports etc.,). It came to our
notice that technical staff are working in shifts and always working in late hours for backup,
file upload and report generation activities.

In view of the above, it is requested to provide the specific information of the offices
under your jurisdiction are not required the outsourced technical manpower and they
could manage the IT related work with existing technical manpower.

It is also requested that the said information may be sent by 29" August, 2012 for
assessing the total manpower requirement to the field offices. Any new ideas and
suggestion in this regard is highly invited.

Yours faithfully,

(B.K.PANDA)
Additional Central PF Commissioner (IS & Project)

Subject: Service to the EPF Subscribers — Performance review of Maharashtra state.
Sir,

It is noticed that during last few months, service to subscribers has considerably
improved in EPFO over the previous years. Most of the field offices have contributed
significantly to this improvement despite various local constraints. This all has been made
possible owing to several factors such as technological advancement, rationalization of office
processes and collaborative response of field offices and Headquarters.

2. However, it has been observed that the performance of Maharashtra state on the whole
is not up to the expected level. The pendency in service to subscribers’ area in Maharashtra
state is also pulling down the national average of performance of EPFO. The situation is
indicative of the fact that a lot needs to be done by the field offices located in Maharashtra. In
this background, some administrative reshuffle has also been carried out recently in the state.

3. In view of the above, it is decided to constitute a Committee to monitor, review and
suggest suitable measures for field offices in Maharashtra state so that present level of
performance could be enhanced to the level where Maharashtra state would also contribute
meaningfully to the overall performance of EPFO. Members of the above Committee are as
under:-

1) Financial Advisor & Chief Accounts Officer
2) Additional Central P.F. Commissioner (MH & CG)
3) Regional P.F. Commissioner — I (Finance & Accounts), Head Office

4. The committee will continuously monitor the progress of Maharashtra field offices and
put up report to CPFC periodically.

(Issues with the approval of CPFC)

further, the fortnight beginning 20" August to 3 September is observed as “Communal
Harmony Fortnight” every year.

administrative control with a view to spreading the message of Sadbhavana and

Subject:- Clarification regarding Language Option for all Departmental Examinations /
Probationary Examinations-reg.
Sir,
Certain references have been received as to whether a candidate may give separate
language option (Hindi or English) for each paper i.e. paper wise option or has to give single option in
respect of all papers in a departmental examination.

The above said matter has been examined and it is clarified that Chapter 8 of Hand Book
for Departmental examination provides the following:-

“The candidates are reguired to give a specific option for a language in their application
wherever the option is allowed. Option once exercised is final and the answer written in the
language other than the one opted will not be valued. The candidates are permitted to opt
for Hindi / English / Regional Language in respect of each paper wherever the option is
allowed. However, the English paper is required to be written only in English. The APFC /
EO, AAO/ Suptd. /LDC (probationers) and the candidates for EO/AAO & Supdt. Examination
may opt for Hindi or English only”

From the above it is clear that the candidates can opt either Hindi or English language
for each paper except Paper I which is the English Paper and is required to be answered in English
only. However, the option once exercised is final and the answer written in the language other than
the one opted will not be valued. This is for information and necessary action of all.

{This issues with the approval of ACC (HR)}

Yours faithfully,

Sub: ‘Training Programme for Liaison Officers(24-28 September,2012) — Nomination(s) Regarding.

Sir,

The National Academy for Training and Research in Social Security (NATRSS) is conducting a five
days Training Programme for Liaison Officers scheduled to be held from 24-28 September,2012 in its
premises at30-31 Institutional Area, D-Block, Janak Puri, New Delhi-110058.
The programme aims at refreshing the knowledge and skills of liaison officers.

The course will broadly cover the following topics:

e Describe Constitutional provisions relating to reservation in service
Identify scope and applicability of reservation orders

List the role and functions of Liaison Officers

Process Reservation in Direct Recruitment and Promotion Cases
Process cases of de-reservation, carry forward, backlog; and

Prepare, operate and maintain reservation rosters

Describe the provisions governing various concessions in appointments.

You are requested to nominate RPFC-II(Adm.) or APFC(Adm.) from your region for this
programme. It may also be ensured that no officer who is retiring in this financial year is nominated. It
should be ensured that the officer nominated by you brings the original set of Reservation Roster
pertaining to your region along with him/her during this training programme.

The name of the nominated officer may please be communicated latest by 27.08.2012.

The accommodation in the hostel will be available from one day before the commencement of the
programme till one day after the completion of the training programme. Any extension beyond this will
require specific approval of Director, NATRSS.

You are requested to relieve the officer(s) with a direction to report to NATRSS on 24.09.2012 at
9.30 A.M. sharp.

Sub: Clarification regarding legal fees payable to panel counsel of EPFAT,

Various High Courts and CAT -—Regarding.

Sir,

A number of references have been received. by the Head Office seeking
clarification on the payment of legal fees to the panel advocates. The matter has
been examined and following clarification is issued to all the field offices for
regulating the fees of panel counsels.

2. In this regard, all the offices are aware that the fees of panel advocates are
paid in accordance to the guidelines issued from time to time by Department of Legal
Affairs, Ministry of Law and Justice treating our panel counsel at par with Central
Government Counsel /Central Government Standing Counsel /Central Government
Panel Counsel. In view of the recent Office Memorandums issued by Ministry of Law
and Justice including No.26 (1)2011-Judl dated 1.9.2011 and circulated vide
H.O.letter No.LC/2/Information/2006 dated 24.1.2012 it is further clarified that this
circular is guiding the fees only for Senior Central Government Panel Counsels for
various High Courts and CAT Benches, who in case of our offices may be engaged in
selected cases of importance.

3. The payment of fees to EPFO panel advocates in Various High
Courts/CAT/Tribunal including Delhi High Court and except Bombay and Kolkata, shall
continue to be regulated at par with the fee structure of Central Govt. Counsel /Panel
Counsel of High Courts as prescribed vide Office memorandum No. 26(1)2005-Jud!
dated 31.1.2008 of Ministry of Law and Justice, which has not been revised.

4. The payment of fees to EPFAT Panel advocates has to be made at par with
the fee payable to advocates before the CAT which is at par with the High Court as
per enclosed Head Office Circular No.LC/3/9/96/MH/7581 dated 19.4.1999(copy
enclosed) and which may be regulated as per revised O.M.No.26(1)2005-Judl. Dated
31.1.2008.

Subject : Withdrawal of power delegated to RPFCS In-charge of
Regional/Sub Regional Offices to grant relaxation under Para 79
of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme,1952-regarding.

Sir,

The Government of India has brought out an amendment in the Finance Act, 2006
introducing clause 56 making it mandatory for all the Provident Fund Trusts recognized
under Income Tax Act, 1961 to obtain exemption under Section 17 of the Employees’
Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act,1952 and the recognition to such fund
shall be withdrawn if the conditions set out in the said clause are not satisfied on or before
the 31% day of March, 2013. The amendment has, in reality, conferred upon Employees’
Provident Fund Organisation the status of a regulator of all Provident Funds. Consequent
upon such amendment, grant of relaxation under,Para 79 of the Employees Provident Fund
Scheme, 1952 has become redundant.

2. Ministry of Labour & Employment has directed to consider withdrawing the power of
relaxation granted to RPFCs In-charge of Regional/Sub Regional Offices since such
relaxation will not enable the Trusts to claim any benefits under the Income Tax Act, 1961
without being exempted under Section 17 of the Act. Further it may also open the door for
future litigation in the matter. It was also pointed out that in a majority of cases relaxation
is granted by the concerned Provident Fund Offices for years together without referring the
matter to the Appropriate Government.

Page 1 of 2

3. In view of above, powers delegated to RPFCs In-charge of Regional Offices/SubRegional Offices to grant relaxation to any establishment under Para 79 of the Employees’
Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 stands withdrawn with immediate effect. This supersedes
the instructions contained in circular No. C-II/Misc./2(06)/Ex/EZ/88651 dated
09/3/2007(copy enclosed) and instructions issued vide letter No. C-II/Misc/02/06/Exem/VolI dated 27.04.2009 stands amended to that extent accordingly.

Yours Faithfully.

Sub:- Seeking support of Regional Offices in Staff Capacity Development- reg.

Sir,

As you are aware Zonal Training Institute, WZ at Ujjain is a Staff Capacity Development Facility
which caters to 11 Regional Offices under the jurisdiction of West Zone. The Institute conducts Induction
& Refresher courses for the staff & Workshops for members of unexempted/exempted establishments. At
an average around sixty programs are held in the Institute on annual basis.

The Institute is making all out efforts to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the programs
and develop the ambience of the Institute. The Institute is, however, facing.enormous difficulties in
arranging faculties for the various programs. In absence of in-house faculty, most of the training sessions
are taken by visiting faculties either drawn from RO Indore or retired officials residing in Indore. In order
to tide over the situation, Regional Commissioner’s of WZ were requested to forward the name of the
officers who are willing to take training sessions. However the response till date has not been encouraging.
It is becoming almost impossible to effectively run the training programs in absence of adequate
faculty resources.

In order to broad base the faculty support and reduce the over dependence on RO, Indore, it
is proposed that each Regional Offices should contribute in lending faculty support to the Zonal
Training Institute. The training courses of the Institute are concentrated from April to February, March
being a lean period in view of avoiding staff movement during financial closing. Thus the faculty issue of
the Institute will be adequately addressed if each Regional Office provides faculty support for a month
in the entire calendar year. This practice will increase the involvement of all Regional Offices in
improving the learning and the development of their staff members. It will go a long way in improving the
operational efficiency of the staff members and productivity of the field offices.

In view of the above Regional Commissioners are kindly requested to offer their views on the
proposition of the Institute. In case, the Regional Commissioners are favorable to the proposition in
principle, the details of sharing modality will be worked out under the leadership of the Director,
NATRSS and respective Regional Commissioners and ACC of the Zone.

Kindly accord priority.
Yours faithfully
(Dr. J.P.Upadhyay)
RPFC-I

Subject:- Updating daily status of backup, recovery, security measures In Centralized
Tool-reg.

Reference:- |S-Doc/1(1)2010/98070-98280 dated 17.02.2011.

Sir,

As you are aware the new application software has been implemented in the
field Offices and all the major service delivery operations are being carried out through
the new system,

The smooth functioning and productivity of an office is dependent upon the
uninterrupted operation of the IT infrastructure deployed in the offices whereas the
systems integrity, reliability and resistance is dependent on adherence to the basic
security and backup protocols that have already been communicated.

Instructions have been issued earlier for setup of severs in failover mode and
end of day synchronization of data between primary and secondary servers as well as
taking regular backups so that In the event of failure or unforeseen eventualities the
systems can be recovered and office operations restored with minimum disruption and
loss of data.

Given the criticality of ensuring system uptime and observance of scheduled
daily activities are online system has been develaped to maintain a centralized inventory
of IT infrastructure at log of daily activities for each office for tracking and monitoring
purposes.

The comprehensive tool has been developed and dovetailed in the “Centralized
Attendance Tracking System” for the outsourced IT personnel.

Necessary instructions may kindly be issued to technical officials and/or
outsourced technical manpower to update the hardware information and log daily
activities backup, recovery etc., in the centralized tool. This tool will make it possible to
monitor the server functionality, backup, recovery on second server, MPLS connectivity
etc., at local, Regional, Zonal and Central level.

A help document on the operation of the software test has been prepared and is
enclosed to understand the functionality of the software. Concerned technical person
may be advised to strictly ensure updation daily log entry in the software.

Training Institute, West Zone. The workshop is meant for EPF Members, Employers & Employers
Representatives with a course fee of Rs. 3000/-.

responsibilitie assigned as per the provisions laid down under EPF & MP Act 1952 and the

of the subscribers, By this Workshop the level of Knowledge of the participants/subscribers will be
enhanced and they will know the quantum of benefits available to them under the schemes and also
their rights and privileges.

providing working lunch, tea, snacks and course materials. One copy of Nomination Form is
enclosed. The fee is to be paid by crossed Demand Draft/ Bankers Cheque drawn in favour of Zonal
Training Institute, West Zone payable at Ujjain

. cannot be successful and sufficient number of participants may not be available. Hence you are
requested to contact the employers of covered establishments as well as Trade Unions within your
jurisdiction and forward at least_03 number of nominations by 09-08-2012 for the above
mentioned Workshop.

Sub: Special Recovery Drive from 01.08.2012 to 30.09.2012.

Sir,

The increasing trend of arrears of Provident Fund and allied dues has become a
matter of great concern. So much so, the performance in recovery of current and arrear dues
is far below the targets fixed by the Headquarters which is not at all appreciable. The C&AG
of India which recently conducted Performance Audit for the period from 2006-07 to 2010-11
observed that the contribution due and arrears to be recovered from the establishments has
been mounting on one hand and recovery thereof shows a downward trend on the other.

2. The all India performance in regard to recovery of dues for the last three years
starting from 2009-10 to 2011-12 (Region-wise) has been circulated for information of all
concerned vide this office letter No. RRC-III/13(228)/Circular/2012 dated 07.06.2012 posted
at the official website of EPFO at SI. No. 159.

ai Similarly the all India performance for the current year upto May, 2012 as per Annual

Business Plan shows poor pace of recovery which is not acceptable and which is a matter of
great concern.

Pagelof5

4. In order to augment recovery, it is decided that a special Recovery Drive shall be
carried out from 01.08.2012 to 30.09.2012 (both un-exempted and exempted sector).

5. The following points shall be kept in mind while conducting the Special Recovery

Drive:

a) Instructions issued vide this office letter No. 19.06.2012 (placed at website at

SI. No. 187) should be adhered to scrupulously.

b) Maximum number of Enforcement Officers, as far as practicable, shall be

C)

detailed to carry out such drive without disturbing other functional areas. The
Enforcement Officers before proceeding in the matter shall gather all
information viz. details of bank accounts, details of Sundry debtors etc. from
the records available in the office and also from third party source like Income
Tax Department, Inspector of Factories and Boilers’, Inspector of Shops and
Establishment, Employees’ State Insurance Corporation, Regional Transport
Authorities, Industries and Commerce Departments, Industrial Estates, Local
Bodies, Co-operative Department, Director of Mining and Geology, Employers’
Associations, Trade Unions etc.

RPFCs, In-charge of Regional Offices / Sub Regional Offices may monitor the
progress of recovery during the currency of the drive on weekly basis and
action plan accordingly may be prepared for following week(s). Necessary
actions against non-performing officers / officials may be initiated and informed
to Headquarters.

d) Wide publicity may be given on such launching of the Special Recovery Drive

through local newspapers, display on the notice boards of the office
prominently, through employer’s associations and trade unions (Sample
advertisement enclosed).

e) The performance of the Regions during the drive in recovery of current and

arrear dues must be reported Offices-wise by the RPFCs In-charge of the
Regions in the Annexures enclosed on a monthly basis for Un-exempted and
Exempted sectors separately to Head Office by 5" of the following month
without fail.

Sub: Procedure of Sanction of leave for Audit Parties.

Sir,
It has been observed that leaves for sanction are being sent to Head Quarters for all
the Audit personnel which is a wrong practice. Henceforth the sanction of leave is regulated

in the following manner as mentioned below.
Nature of Leave Sanctioning Authori
Deputy Director | All kind of leaves Director Audit

Assistant Director Concemed Deputy Director

Audit Earned Leave / Commuted | Director Audit
Leave/other leave

Casual leave Concemed AD (OIC of IAP)

Earned Leave / Commuted | Concemed Deputy Director

1. Sanction of leave is not a matter of right. The leave sanctioning authority can reject
the sanction of leave without assigning any reason. .

2. In no case the team members shall go on leave without pre-sanction. In case of
extreme emergencies, telephonic permission may be sought from the leave
sanctioning Authority and the same may be recorded on the face of leave
application while forwarding the same.

3. No official is permitted to extend the leave already sanctioned under any reason. All
the leave applications should be complete in all respects and should contain the
complete Postal Address, land line residential Telephone No. wherever available
and Mobile No.

4. A Register containing the details of all the leave taken and date of forwarding of the
leave application to the Head Office and the IAP Headquarters Office for all the
Members of the Audit Team as stated above with due attestation of the senior most

Assistant Director (Audit) is required to be maintained. The Register is liable for
verification whenever the Officers from Head Office inspects the Audit Team at the
camp stations.

5. Inno case, the absence of team members be an excuse for extension of the camp
period. A maximum of one person shall only be on leave at a time to ensure smooth
completion of the Audit activities. The Deputy Directors / Assistant Directors in
Charge shall be personally responsible to ensure timely completion of the Audit
work by acting as the team leader and ensuring that no unwarranted interference is
made with the working of the team. Whenever the leaves are sanctioned by Head
Office, the same will be communicated to controlling Headquarters for necessary
record in the Service Books. In case of absence by any team member without
sanction of leave, the controlling Headquarters may not draw pay for the period till
clear permission is granted by Audit Wing of Head Office.

6. No official / Officer is permitted to proceed on leave in case of EL without the
sanction of the competent authority. The E.L. application for sanction should be
submitted much before the date of leave so that the leave sanctioning authority will
have sufficient time for sanction of leave.

All concemed are directed to strictly adhere to the above directions.
Yours faithfully
ANN

(P.C.PATI)
Director (Audit)

INSTRUCTIONS FOR CANDIDATES

All candidates are directed to go through the following instructions before the examination as failure to
comply with the instructions will render the candidates liable for disciplinary action, as deemed fit, apart
from being debarred from the examination.

1) No candidate shall be admitted to the examination hall after half an hour of the commencement of the
examination.

2) No candidate shal! leave the Examination Hall without prior permission of the Supervisor / Invigilator.

3) No candidate shall be permitted to leave the Examination Hall unti} an hour has elapsed after the
commencement of the Examination.

4) No candidate shail normally be permitted to visit toitets during first and last half an hour of the
examination.

S) The candidate, after finishing his/her examination, shall continue to sit at his/her desk and wait until
his/her answer book is collected. He/she must not write or revise his/her answers after the expiry of the
allotted time.

The candidates must remain in their seats until thelr answer books have been collected by the
supervising officer / invigilator.

The candidates are required to take drinking water from the water jug placed inside the examination hail.
Candidates must observe silence in the Examination Hall. Smoking in the Examination Hall is strictly
prohibited,

The question paper supplied to a candidate should not be taken out of the examination hall during the
course of examination. While visiting toilet, the answer book and the Question Paper should be kept on
the table face-down and informed to the invigilator/supervisor.

10) The candidates should produce their identity cards - both office and examination | cards before the
Supervisor, Board of Examination for verification.

11) The candidate should bring his own writing material like pen, pencil and scale as may be required for the
examination. The Board of Examination will supply the necessary Question Papers, Answer Books,
Continuation Sheets, Tags etc. relevant for the examination.

12) The candidate shall not be permitted to bring any article other than those specified above, such as books,
notes, loose sheets, printed or written material & calculatar, cell phone, pagers or any other electronic’
devices etc. Into the examination hall. Bags, Handbags, luggage, etc. should be kept outside the
Examination Hall. (Wherever the use of books Is permitted the same shall be verified by the Supervisor
$0 as to ensure that the books brought by the candidates are as specified in the syllabus without any
notes / annotations typed, written or pasted therein. Authorized amendments are however permitted.

13) The candidate must write in the Answer Books in his own hand in ink. In no circumstances will he/she be
allowed to take the help of any one to write answers for him/her. Answers must not be written In pencil,
pencil may, however, be used for rough work, etc.

14) The candidate must write only his/her roll number and not his/her name in the space provided for the
purpose on roll no. slip of the answer book which he/she uses. He/she must not write any irrelevant
matter inside his/her answer book i.e. anything other than the actual answer to questions, such as appeal
to the examiner for marks, criticism of question paper, etc. Candidate must not write his/her rofl no. or
name / code of the regional / sub-regional office / centre even in answer to a question on letter writing.
Any answer book in which the name or roll No. or Regional / Sub-Regional Office code has been written,
will not be evaluated.

15) If a candidate uses more than one continuation sheet, he/she should state on the front page of the
answer book the total number of continuation sheets he/she has used. The candidate must tag all the
continuation sheets supplied to him/her for answering questions, whether used or not, and fasten them

securely before handing over to the invigilators. Candidates should strike off blank sheets before
submitting the answer sheets.

ABOUT ZONAL TRAINING INSTITUTE
(NORTH ZONE)

The Zonal Training Institute, North Zone,
Faridabad-now known as Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee
Institute of Social Security Administration (SPMISSA),
was set up in the year 1993 under the administrative
control of National Academy for Training & Research in
Social Security (NATRSS), New Delhi to meet the
challenges of Human Resource Development in
Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO),
Ministry of Labour & Employment, Govt. of India. This
Institute is primarily meant for imparting training to the
EPFO Staff in North Zone covering, Head Office
(Delhi), Delhi, Haryana, Himachal Pardesh, Punjab,
Uttar Pardesh & Uttaranchal.

Employee’s Provident Fund Organisation is the
world’s largest publicly managed Social Security
Organisation administring Provident Funds & Providing
Pension benefits to the persons employed in the Public
and Private Sector in India except State of Jammu &
Kashmir. It operates three Schemes viz Employees’
Provident Fund Scheme, 1952, Employees’ Pension
Scheme, 1995 (replacing Employees’ Family Pension
Scheme, 1971) and Employees’ Deposit-Linked
Insurance Scheme, 1976.

The Zonal Training Institute, North Zone, Faridabad
under direction and advice of the NATRSS_ has
undertaken the task of apprising, in stages, the members,
employees and employers, of the establishments
covered under the Employees’ Provident Fund Act about
the object and salient provisions of the PF Act & the
Schemes framed thereunder with a view to ensure
effective implementation of the Schemes for extending
benefits and social security to the working classes
through Seminars, Workshops at lowest possible cost.

The Zonal Training Institute North Zone
(SPMISSA) Faridabad is housed in its own complex
since 10th June ‘02 and is having sufficient expertise,
space and infrastructure for arranging one or more
training courses simultaneously for the Employers of
covered establishment / EPF Members or the members
of Board of Trustee of Exempted Establishments in the
above Regions. The institute has organised numerous
workshops and seminars every calender year since
2003-04, There has been unprecedented response to all
workshops and seminars organised for the benefit of
employers as well as employees of establishments
covered under EPF & MP Act, 1952.

Subject: Deduction of Intercity charges from Regional Accounts by Link

Sir,

It has come to the notice of Head Office that some Link branches of SBI are
deducting intercity charges for Inter departmental transfers from the Bank Accounts of
Regional/Sub- Regional Offices which is not in conformity with the Banking Agreement
between EPFO & SBI.

N

The relevant clauses for Service Charges payable to SBI as per the

Agreement between EPFO & SBI are reproduced below:

Para 5.11: “The service charges @Rs.3.00 per Rs.1,000/- on the total monies
received by the Base Branch on behalf of the Trustees and remitted to the Link branch is
payable to the Link branch of SBI by the concerned Regional/Sub-Regional Office every
month, This will be inclusive of cost of transfer of money from the Base branches to the
concerned Link branch like postage/courier, telegram etc.’

Para 5.12: ‘The service charges @Rs.3.00 per Rs.1,000/- on the monies received
directly on behalf of Trustees is payable to the Link branch of SBI by the concerned
Regional/Sub Regional Office’

Para 5.17: “Levy of charges shall be only on collection of dues and remittances
from Base branches to Link branches and on dues directly collected by the Link
branches. There shall not be any charge on _ other inter departmental
remittances/transfers (i.e. money transferred from one bank account to another bank
account of the Trustees maintained with SBI at difference places). Contribution collected
under VDR and submitted to branches under ‘New Process’ will not be treated as interdepartmental transfers and usual charges will be levied for such collections.’

The Agreement entered into between EPFO & SBI on 07.10.2010 is available at
Sr. No. 282 of 2010-11 of Office Orders & Circular on official website of EPFO.

3. In view of above, all Regional/Sub-Regional Offices are requested to verify their
Bank Accounts (A/c No. i, 2, i0, 2i & 22) and if any intercity charges have been
deducted by link branch for Inter departmental transfers, the matter may be taken up with

concerned Link branch to revert/credit back the amount to concerned EPFO Accounts.

Sub:
Recovery of Arrear Dues.
Sir,
The increasing trend of arrears of Provident Fund and allied dues has become a matter of
great concern. In order to ensure speedy recovery of arrear dues (both under exempted and unexempted sector),all the Regional Provident Fund Commissioners and Assistant Provident Fund
Commissioners have been notified as Recovery Officers way back in early 1997 vide Head Office
Circular
No.RRC/8(9)96/RM/13531-45
dated
19.03.1997
and
Notification
No.
S.O 796
dated
04.03.1997 was published in Part II,
Section 3, Sub-section (ii) of the Gazette of India dated
22.03.1997 to that effect. The information available at Head Office reveals that the performance
regarding recovery of arrears have not been satisfactory and there is need for an "Action Plan" for
effective recovery.
2.
In order to maximize recovery, the following procedures must be strictly ensured:
a) All actions as required under Section 86 to 8G of the EPF& MP Act, 1952 and under
IInd Schedule of the Income Tax Act, 1961 have been taken in respect of all RRCs
received from Assessing Officer at the close of financial year by 31st March.
b) Prosecution cases in respect of chronic and habitual defaulters
are filed in the
appropriate Courts well within the time and followed vigorously.
Page 1 of 4

c)
Action under Section 406/409 I.P.c. has been taken in all eligible cases and cases
already filed with Police Authorities are pursued vigorously excepting in case of Public
Sector Undertakings of Central and State Governments.
d) Applications for vacation of Stay granted by High Courts have been filed in true spirit
and perspective.
e)
In
view
of the
Hon'ble Supreme Court judgment
in SLP No.
15243/2007 and
20736/2007
in the
matter
of
Maharashtra State Co-operative
Bank Limited Vs.
Assistant Provident Fund Commissioner and Ors.(2009)10 SCC 123 wherein the issue
of priority of dues has been decisively upheld as provided under Section 11(2) of the
EPF&MP Act,1952,
all cases held up in various courts and categorized as 'Not
Immediately
Realizable' may be taken up for scrutiny and get those disposed off
favorably
so as to ensure speedy recovery of locked up statutory
dues. (Copy
enclosed).
f)
In cases of establishments which are under liquidation, necessary claims incorporating
up to date dues i.e., current as well as arrears are filed with the Official Liquidators in
time. For favorable disposal of cases of this nature the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme
Court in CA NO. 9630 of 2011 arising out of SLP(Civil) No. 7642 of 2011 in the matter
of Employees' PF Commissioner Vs. O.L. of Esskay Pharmaceuticals Ltd. dated 8.11.11
wherein even in liquidation, priority of EPFdues have been granted, may be relied on
aggressively. (Copy enclosed).
g)
Further
Directors of the Company are personally liable for the PF dues of the
employees in their personal capacity even if they cease to be Directors of Company
upon winding of the Company. In this regard judgement
in Special Civil Application
19075 of 2007 of Hon. High Court of Gujarat may be relied upon.
In all such cases,
actions under Section 88 1 (a) (b) and (c) of the EPF& MP Act, 1952 may be invoked
which are independent to each other for speedy recovery. (Copy enclosed).
h) In winding up cases pending in Company Court where final outcome generally takes
long time, applications may be filed before the Company Court to sell limited assets of
the defaulting establishment for speedy recovery of statutory EPFdues. In this regard
judgement
of Hon. High Court of Karnataka in Company Petition No. 79 of 1980
between S.M. Holding Finance Pvt. Limited Vs. Mysore Machinery Manufacturers Ltd.
(In Liquidation) may be relied upon. (Copy enclosed).

Subject: Transfer of RTI applications under Section 6(3) of the RTI Act 2005 —
Instructions regarding.
Sir,
In certain cases, RTI applications received by the CPIO (Finance) at Head Office wherein
the information sought by the applicant relates to the field offices are transferred to the concerned
CPIOs under section 6(3) of the RIT Act 2005, for providing the information directly to the

applicant.

In this regard, it is observed that in many cases the concerned CPIOs, while providing
information to the applicant endorses a copy to CPIO (Finance), for information. Endorsing a copy
of information to CPIO (Finance) does not serve any purpose at our end and at the same time

increases the avoidable correspondence with the Head Office.

Therefore, the CPIOs are requested to provide the information directly to the applicants
and not to endorse the copy of the information to CPIO (Finance), if not requested specifically.

[This issues with the approval of CPIO (Finance), Head Office].

Subject: Verification of settled claims — Regarding.
Sir,

It has come to the notice of Head Office that a fictitious claim has been settled
fraudulently through VDR special entry in a field office.

2. The preliminary information available in this matter revealed that the Dealing
Assistant (DA) processed the claim at all stages himself by forged signature and misuse of
login password of the Authorizing Officer under VDR special entry. Accordingly, he managed
to get the amount credited in the Saving Bank Account of his wife through NEFT.

3. In this background, it is requested to carry out the following exercise in your office:-

(A) Settlement of claims under Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) Scheme

i) Prepare a list of Bank accounts of EPF members wherein two or more payments
have been made during the year 2011-12.

ii) Simultaneously prepare a list of EPF Accounts from where two or more
payments have been authorised during the year 2011-12.

(B) Settlement of claims under Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS)

i) Prepare a list of Bank accounts of EPS members wherein two or more payments
have been made during the year 2011-12 for withdrawal benefits.

ii) Simultaneously prepare a list of EPS Accounts from where two or more
withdrawals have been sanctioned during the year 2011-12.

-2-

(C) Settlement of claims under Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance
(EDLI) Scheme

i) Prepare a list of Bank accounts of EPF members wherein two or more
payments have been made during the year 2011-12.

ii) Simultaneously prepare a list of EPF Accounts from where two or more
payments have been authorised during the year 2011-12.

The above exercise may be carried out at your end and then such
settlements/payments be verified for the genuineness of the claim. In case of any
discrepancies noticed, action be taken to rectify those discrepancies under intimation to
Head Office.

4. In addition to the above, it is also requested that suitable instructions be issued at
your level to all the concerned, regarding protection of individual password of each official.
It may be brought to the notice of all concerned, that system login password is a
CONFIDENTIAL information and must not be shared with any other person. This is also to
be ensured that officials should change their login password at regular intervals. Further, in
case of any misuse of login password of any official by any other person, it would be the
responsibility of the concerned official to whom the said login password has been allotted.

5. An action taken report be forwarded to Head Office by 10.07.2012 positively.

OFFICE MEMORANDUM

Subject: Grant of Dearness Relief to Central Government
pensioners/family pensioners - Revised rate effective
from 1.1.2012.

The undersigned is directed to refer to this Department’s
OM No. 42/15/2011-P&PW(G) dated 5'” October, 2011 on the subject
mentioned above and to state that the President is pleased to decide
that the Dearness Relief (DR) payable to Central Government
pensioners/family pensioners shall be enhanced from the existing rate
of 58% to 65% w.e.f. 1* January, 2012.

2. These orders apply to (i) All Civilian Central Government
Pensioners/Family Pensioners (ii) The Armed Forces Pensioners, Civilian
Pensioners paid out of the Defence Service Estimates, (iii) All India
Service Pensioners (iv) Railway Pensioners and (v) The Burma Civilian
pensioners/family pensioners and pensioners/families of displaced
Government pensioners from Pakistan, who are Indian Nationals but
receiving pension on behalf of Government of Pakistan and are in receipt
of ad-hoc ex-gratia allowance of Rs. 3500/- p.m. in terms of this
Department’s OM No. 23/1/97-P&PW(B) dated 23.2.1998 read with this
Department's OM No. 23/3/2008-P&PW(B) dated 15.9.2008.

3. Central Government Employees who had drawn lumpsum
amount on absorption in a PSU/Autonomous body and have become
eligible to restoration of 1/3 commuted portion of pension as well as
revision of the restored amount in terms of this Department's OM No.
4/59/97-P&PW (D) dated 14.07.1998 will also be entitled to the payment
of DR @ 65% w.e.f. 1.1.2012 on full pension i.e. the revised pension
which the absorbed employee would have received on the date of
restoration had he not drawn lumpsum payment on absorption and
Dearness Pension subject to fulfillment of the conditions laid down in para
5 of the O.M. dated 14.07.98. In this connection, instructions contained
in this Department’s OM No.4/29/99-P&PW (D) dated. 12.7.2000 refer.

4, Payment of DR involving a fraction of a rupee shall be
rounded off to the next higher rupee.

Subject: Compliance in respect of International Workers —
regarding.

Sir,

Special Provisions in respect of International Workers included in
the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 as well as Employees’
Pension Scheme, 1995 have been given effect from 1% October, 2008.
Subsequently, certain amendments have also been carried out vide
notification dated 11" September, 2010 and the same were circulated vide
Head Office letter No. Coord/5(15)/2009/IW/07733 dated 25/26"
November, 2010. In pursuance of these amendments detailed instructions
were issued vide this office letter No.IWU/7(6)2007/41959 dated gh
September, 2009 and No.IWU/7(11)/Compliance dated 30"August, 2011.

2. Representations have been received by this office seeking clarity
on the status of International Workers (IWs), The matter has been
reviewed holistically in the light of special provisions contained in para 83
of EPF Scheme, 1952 and para 43-A of EPS, 1995 and accordingly the
position is clarified as under:

i. The category of IWs will comprise only those Indian employees who
have contributed to the social security programme of a country
having SSA with India and having gained or going to gain eligibility
for benefits under the said SSA only, and their contribution,
membership to the Fund etc, will be regulated by special provisions
contained in para 83 of EPF Scheme, 1952 and para 43-A of
EPS,1995.

ii. | The detached employee, who avails exemption from contributing in
the other country by obtaining a Certificate of Coverage (COC) from
India and contributes to the social security system in India, will not
fall under the category of IW. However, it would be mandatory for
him to contribute as a member in India, which is a pre-requisite for
COC.

iii. All employees holding other than Indian passport, employed in an
establishment covered under the Act, and who do not hold COC, will
contribute as IWs.

3. The other matters in respect of such IWs will be regulated as
under:

i. With effect from 1* October, 2008 each and every IW, other than
an ‘excluded employee’ is required to be a member of the
Employees’ Provident Fund.

il. A detached IW contributing to the social security programme of
the home country and certified as such by a valid COC issued by
the country of origin for a specified period in terms of the bilateral
SSA signed between that country and India is an ‘excluded
employee’.

iii. The contribution in respect of all IWs is required to be paid by the
employer on full salary (i.e. without any wage ceiling) as per
provisions of the scheme.

iv. The components of salary to be included for the purpose of

Subject: Payment of PF accumulations after closure of establishment, in absence of
Form 3A/6A.
Sir,

May kindly refer to the subject cited above. As you are aware that the establishments
covered under the EPF and MP Act, 1952 are required to remit provident fund contribution on
monthly basis in respect of all the eligible employees. However, till 31.03.2012 (Before introduction
of ECR) the contributions were reflected in the member’s account only after receiving details of
subscription in Annual Returns i.e. 3A and 6A. At times, these returns were not submitted by the
employers of the closed establishments although the PF office was in receipt of contributions by
way of monthly remittances or recovery of the amount in default. The compliance measures
initiated against such establishments to procure the returns, many a times did not yield result due

to non-traceability of either the employers or the records. This finally results in non-payment of PF
accumulations to the members.

In order to mitigate the hardship to members to claim their PF accumulation in above
situation a proposal was placed before the CBT, EPF in its 193% meeting held on 30.03.2011. The
CBT, EPF in the said meeting approved the proposed scheme, which is to be known as
‘Disbursement Scheme’.

DISBURSEMENT SCHEME

Two major categories of establishments have been identified where the credit of
contribution to the members’ account and its disbursement is to be processed in the scheme:-

A) The establishments which have earlier submitted the Form 3A or 6A but have
discontinued later,
B) The establishments, which have never submitted the Form 3A or 6A.

Since in existing framework of the Act and Scheme, where provisions for protecting
member's interest has been laid down quite rigidly and no apparent solution was available to the
above problem, following action are suggested: -

i) For establishments, indicated in point A) above:

a) The last return (3A or 6A) submitted by the employer may be taken as base document
for crediting the balance amount into members’ accounts.

b) The amount recovered may be divided proportionately amongst the members whose
names appeared in the above said return, after consultation with the concerned
employer and workers’ representatives, wherever possible.

c) After completing, the action described in point (a) & (b) above, the proposal may be
placed before the Regional Committee for approval.

d) The Regional Committee, after satisfying itself that due diligence has been exercised by
the PF office and the Employer, and the details of the employees cannot be retrieved
through routine process, it will consider the proposal submitted by the PF office for
approval.

e) After approval by the Regional Committee, the scheme of disbursing the recovered
amount amongst the members may be published in the local newspaper with the names
of beneficiaries with specific mention that if any other person who considers that his
interest has not been taken care of in the said scheme may file his objection within 30
days from the date of publication of such scheme.

f) If no objections are filed within the specified period, the intended amount may be
disbursed amongst the members covered in the said scheme otherwise the revised
disbursement may be made if the claim of the member filing objection is accepted.

ii) For establishments, indicated in point B) above:

a) The concerned PF office may publish a Public Notice in a local newspaper to the effect
that any person who claims to have worked in the said establishment during the
specified period, may submit the proof of his period of employment and wages drawn
to that PF office, with in 30 days from the publication of the Notice so that he could be
considered for being listed as PF beneficiary, and his entitlements.

b) After expiry of the notice period, the details of the persons who have proved their
employment and wages drawn in that establishment beyond doubt, may be prepared in
consultation with employer’s and worker’s representative, wherever possible, for placing
the proposal for disbursement before the Regional Committee.

c) The Regional Committee, after satisfying itself that necessary records cannot be
retrieved with due diligence, may approve the above proposal for disbursing the
accumulations amongst the employees so selected.

Any amount remaining undisbursed after the said exercise may be transferred to Special
Reserve Fund for meeting out any future contingency in this regard.

The Disbursement Scheme as stated above is circulated herewith to the field offices for
implementation. Kindly acknowledge the receipt.

Yours faithfully,

oe
(Rajesh Bansal)
Financial Advisor & Chief Accounts Officer

Sub.: Clarification regarding pay fixation in respect of SO/PS on promotion to the
post of APFC- regarding.
: Sir,

Many references have been received with regard to pay fixation in respect of APFCs
promoted from SO/PS cadre and who were earlier granted Non-Functional Scale.

2. In this connection your attention is invited to Head Office letter No.
HRD/1(1)2000/RR/SO/pt.1/49875 dated 04.10.2007, HRD/P-IV/2(4)83/Vol.I1/49896 dated
04.10.2007 and DOP&T Order No. 6/3/2009-CS.I(S) dated 19.11.2009.

3 In view of the above provisions, pay of SO and PS while granting Non Functional
Scale before 01.01.2006 was required to be done under FR 22(1)(a)(2) i.e. only placement in
the next higher grade without increment. After 01.01.2006, the pay of SO and PS are
required to be fixed under Rule 13 of CCS(Revised Pay) Rules 2008 i.e. granting of one
increment at the time of granting Non Functional Scale.

4. Now the question is that whether the one increment will be granted at the time of
promotion in respect of APFCs who are promoted from SO/PS cadre and who were earlier
granted Non Functional Scale. As mentioned above, there may be cases (i.e. before
01.01.2006) where they were not granted one increment at the time of Non-Functional Grade.
In such cases, at the time of promotion, they are entitled for one increment under FR
22(1)(a)(1). There may be the cases (i.e. after 01.01.2006) where one increment was granted
at the time of granting of Non-Functional Scale. In such cases, as one increment was already
provided earlier, their pay will be fixed in accordance with FR 22(1)(a)(2).

5. You are requested to examine these representations at your level in consultation with
Internal Audit. Please see that only one increment will be granted either at the time of
granting Non-Functional Scale or at the time of promotion.

1966 batch IAS and Shri. Navin Chawla for the period 2000 — 07/04/2009, along with related
information pertaining to the handling of his RTI application — enclosed herewith as Annexure
A.

2. The CPIO vide his order of 27/04/2009 denied disclosure under sub section (j) of section
8 (1) of the Act. The applicant preferred appeal dated 18/05/2009 before First Appellate
Authority which was disposed of vide FAAO of 18/06/2009 and upheld the order of the CPIO.

3: Not being satisfied by the above orders the applicant preferred second appeal before the
Commission. The matter was heard today. Both parties were present as above and presented
arguments.

Decision

4. After hearing both parties the Commission upholds the order of the CPIO and the First
Appellate Authority on the grounds that the property returns of the officers as submitted to the
cadre authorities every year in confidence and disclosure of information contained herein would
definitely be unwarranted invasion of the privacy of the individual which is exempted under
section 8 (1) (j) of the RTT Act, 2005.

=) The Commission cannot accept the averments of the appellant that he, as an informed
citizen has the right to such personal information pertaining to persons serving in government
since he would then act to curb corruption. The Commission pointed out to the appellant that if
he had any specific information with regard to any acts of corruption or proportionate wealth in
respect of any civil servant he should pass it on to the designated organisations who are charged
with the responsibility of investigation in such matters. The role of such investigating agencies
cannot be assumed by any citizen along with the right to have access to personal information of

Sir,

This is in continuation to this office letter of even number dated 08.02.2012 and
dated 14.03.2012 on the subject cited above.

Zz: It is observed during the review at Head Office in respect of pendency of claims
that a tangible improvement had taken place in most of the offices at the close of March
2012. However, field offices have failed to maintain the same tempo in the month of
April 2012. It is also observed that even pendency of claims beyond 30 days has also
piled up in sizeable number.

3: Again, in the matter of updation of members’ accounts, same situation prevails
and a huge gap in the performance of March 2012 and April 2012 has been observed.
Field offices have failed to maintain the same drive of disposal on this count also which
was observed in March 2012.

4. Therefore, you are requested to ensure that the tempo of disposal in the matter
of settlement of claims and updation of members’ accounts is maintained by the field
offices as was in the month of March 2012.

5. It is pertinent to mention here that all received Claims, if in order, are to be
settled within 30 days as mandated in the EPF Scheme 1952. Further, after introduction
of ECR (Electronic Challan-cum-Challan), it is important to rise to the occasion taking full
advantage of the new system of ECR and update members’ accounts at the earliest
without waiting for the prescribed time limit i.e. 30° September 2012.

6. It is to highlight that this kind of proactive efforts made by the field offices will go
a long way to facelift the image of the Organisation among its stakeholders in specific
and the public in general.

Subject:- Proper scrutiny of applications for Departmental Examinations - Regarding

Sir,

; It has been observed time and again that the list of candidates is forwarded by the RPFCs for
various Departmental Examinations without proper scrutiny to ensure the eligibility of the candidate so
far as the required service, educational qualification, etc. is concerned. It is also noticed that final list of
candidates duly certified by the RPFC is forwarded with certain “Riders/conditions/requests for
relaxation” etc, which sometimes leads to ineligible candidates appearing for Departmental
Examinations leading to further legal complications.

It is, therefore, requested that all RPFCs In-charge of Regions shall ensure that the eligibility of
each and every candidate is confirmed from the service book of such candidate and only then the final
list be forwarded to Head Office. In case of candidates appearing from the Sub Regional Offices under
jurisdiction of RPFC-I, the required details should be certified by the OIC of such SRO and the relevant
records kept with the Regional Office also for future reference. Any request/representation from
ineligible candidates should be sent separately and in advance so as to take a decision if required.
However, as a general rule, RPFCs may ensure that no relaxation/interpretation of eligibility criteria
should be made without proper confirmation from Head Office.

The above instructions may be strictly followed in respect of all Departmental Examinations.

Subject..- Adoption of the New Pension Scheme applicable to employees of Central
Government, in EPFO as mandated under Section 5D(7) of the EPF & MP Act,
1952.

Sir,

The Central Board of Trustees, Employees’ Provident Fund, in its 190" meeting held
on 15.09.2010 approved the proposal for adoption of New Pension Scheme in respect of
employees appointed on or after 01.01.2004 as required under Section 5 D (7) of the Act and
also authorized the transfer of matching contribution of New Pension Scheme on a monthiy
basis for contribution due and collected from new entrants.

Z: Pending approval from the Board, the instructions were issued vide Head Office
circular No. HRD-3(100)/97/Pt. 84055 dated 17” February, 2005 that officers/officials who
have joined service in the EPFO on or after 01.01.2004 the amount towards the Defined
Contribution Pension Scheme is required to be deducted @ 10% of Basic pay plus Dearness
Allowance from the salary bills every month from 01.01.2004 onwards. The amount so
deducted may be retained in Account No,2/4 of the Organisation as the case may be.

3. Further, following the government instructions, the amount so deducted with matching
contribution and prescribed interest thereon to be deposited/invested through Pension Fund
Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)/NSDL. For the purpose, each Pay &
Accounts Officer/DDO of Field Offices and individual employee has to be registered
individually with the concerned offices of Central Record Keeping Agency (CRA) which is
NSDL, but prior to this EPFO has to APR for registration at the Headquarter level known as
Oversight Office.

4. Further, it is mentioned that the record of the past accumulation deducted as
contribution under head of New Pension Scheme from the monthly salary of the employees
recruited/appointed on or after 01.01.2004 is lying with your offices. The said contribution
was to be intimated/provided at Headquarters Office for calculating the matching contribution
and interest thereon and for the purpose of allocation of budget in the concemed head.
Hence, for the requisite information, a format seeking the details contribution deducted under
New Pension Scheme fram the monthly salary of the officials who were appointed on or after
01,01,.2004 onwards was devised at the Headquarters Office and circulated to all field offices
vide Head Officer circular No.BSC-12(2)-08/40085-40285 dated 22-03-2011 (uploaded in
the EPFO’s website at SI. No. 552 of the last year). While forwarding the
information in the format, it was requested to ensure that the consolidated amount deducted
under New Pension Scheme in each financial year i.e. 2003-04, 2004-05, 2005-06, 2006-07,
2007-08, 2008-09, 2009-10 & 2010-11 should be tallied with the amounts as furnished in your
office's Annual Accounts of each financial year. But on receipt of required data it was
observed that no field office has furnished accurate & correct information. Field offices
informed that errors occurred in the previous years’ Annual Accounts will be rectified in the
Annual Accounts for the years 2011-12.

5. In the matter, it is intimated that action for registration with PFRDA/NSDL has been
initiated at the level of Head Office. On closing of financial year 2011-2012, the Annual
Accounts for the said period are being prepared by your offices. You are, therefore,
requested to provide accurate & correct figures towards contribution deducted from
01.01.2004 onwards under New Pension Scheme in respect of each official wno have been
recruited & joined in the EPF Organisation. If there is any discrepancy, the same may be
rectified in the Annual Accounts for the year 2011-12.

6. Further, it is requested to issue directions to the concerned dealing staff members
who are maintaining SPF Account/Ledger in your office to maintain Account/Ledger in
regards to contribution deducted on account of New Pension Scheme in respect of
officers/officials appointed on or after 01.01.2004 also as the no. of officers/officials appointed
before 01.01.2004 & whose SPF Account is being maintained are gradually decreasing.

Sub: Grant of 72 Installments regarding.
Sir,

As a result of tremendous pressure by way of initiating recovery
proceedings, number of defaulting establishments were approaching the
organization to clear the dues in installments. The matter was placed in the
meeting of the CBT and it was decided to give installment facility to defaulting
establishment but the maximum installment was restricted to 36. The powers to
grant installment facility was enhanced various times but the number of
installment was restricted to only 36.

Requests were being received to grant more than 36 installments. After
giving due consideration, it has been decided by the Central Provident Fund
Commissioner to grant up to 72 installments to clear the outstanding dues only
on following terms & conditions :-

Eligibility
1 Proposal will only be considered in case of un-exempted Establishments.

és Sickness is prevailing in the industry or class of establishment has been
noted and recognized as such by the concerned Ministry.

3. In case of default of employees share, the proposal for installment will not
be considered.

4. The employer shall be informed that grant of installment facility is not
absolving him from the payment of statutory dues under Section 14 B and

7Q.
5. If the establishment has earlier availed the installment facility and has

defaulted as per terms/conditions of installment facility, second application
for the same shall not be considered in this regara.

Meeting Minutes

Essential documents/ requirement
(A) Deferred payment Bank Guarantee issued by the Bank.
OR
(B) Copy of attachment order of the property. The valuation of the same
(immovable) should commensurate with the amount of default for which
installment facility is being considered.
You are requested to examine the proposals for request of 72 installments

in the light of the above terms & conditions and forward the same with your
specific recommendation.

(This issues with approval of Central PF Commissioner)

Sub: Launch of Electronic Return cum Challan (ECR) by Employees’
Provident Fund Organisation-Instructions-regarding.

Please refer to the CPFC DO letter dated 26.03.2012 on the
subject cited above.
The Employer e-Sewa Portal was launched by EPFO by
providing a link through the epfindia website to facilitate collection of
the ECR from the employers on a monthly basis. The portal will also
provide other benefits to the employers.
The details of the Electronic Challan cum Return are as follows.
The Electronic Challan cum Return (ECR) will be an electronic
monthly return that has to be uploaded by the employers by login to
the Employer e-Sewa Portal using the permanent user id and
password created during the process of registration of their
Establishment.
The process of registration of an establishment (with screen
shots) has already been made available on the website. Further in case
any employer finds that his/her establishment has already been
registered, the process of resetting the registration has also been
explained and has been made available on the Admin Portal for the
ECR and one admin user each for the field offices have been provided
with the user id and password.
The admin user will reset the login of the employer if a Request
letter generated from the portal and duly signed by the Employer/

Authorised
Officer
is
received.
The
signature
of
the
employer/authorized signatory is to be verified by the concerned
task holder having the custody of the specimen signature card from
that establishment. It is requested to ensure that that any such
letter received is immediately handled and the resetting is done so
that the employer may register his/her establishment.
The format of the ECR has also been made available on the
website. The return has the fields for monthly wage and contribution
(due and being remitted) details for each member, members details
(as required under the Form 5) in case of members who have joined
during the wage month and the details regarding exit (as required
under the Form 10) for the members who have left service during
the wage month for which the return is uploaded.
From the month of April 2012, when the returns for the wage
month of March 2012 are to be submitted, the employers have to
upload the ECR through the Employer e-Sewa portal.
The complete process flow for the submission of the ECR and
remittance has been explained through screen shots document and
has been made available on the Employer e-Sewa Portal.
The advantages of the new Return are as follows:
1. The employers need not file any paper return from the
month of Wage Month March 2012.
2. The employers will not be required to file the various
monthly and annual returns.
3. The ECR will be linked with the remittance and only such ECR
will reach the field offices where remittance is received. This
will help in auto updation of the members balances once the
remittance of the challan is confirmed in the bank
statement.

OFFICE MEMORANDUM

Subject:— Central Civil Services (Revised Pay) Rules, 2008 ~ Date of next increment in
the revised pay structure under Rule 10 of the CCS(RP) Rules, 2008.

in accordance with the provisions contained in Rule 10 of the CCS (RP) Rules,
2008, there will be a uniform date of annual increment, viz. 1% July of every year.
Employees completing 6 months and above in the revised pay structure as on 1* of July
will be eligible to be granted the increment. The first increment after fixation of pay on
4.1.2006 in the revised pay structure will be granted on 1.7.2006 for those employees
for whom the date of next increment was between 1* July, 2006 to 1* January, 2007.

2. The Staff Side has represented on this issue and has requested that those
employees who were due to get their annual increment between February to June
during 2006 may be granted one increment on 01.01.2006 in the pre-revised scale.

3. On further consideration and in exercise of the powers available under CCS(RP)
Rules, 2008, the President is pleased to decide that in rélaxation of stipulation under
Rule 10 of these Rules, those central government employees who were due to get their

annual increment between February to June during 2006 may be granted one increment
on 1.1.2006 in the pre-revised pay Scale as a one time measure and thereafter will get
